# HCM Next Production TDD Backlog

This is the dependency-ordered delivery backlog for turning the architecture in
[the master plan](plan.md) into a production HCM Next platform. `plan.md` remains
the product and architecture constitution. [The Phase 1 execution plan](execution-plan.md)
controls near-term sequencing and implementation depth. A todo cannot use this
file to expand Phase 1 beyond those authorities.

The backlog deliberately includes later production obligations so they are not
left implicit. Their phase labels prevent them from becoming accidental Phase 1
scope. Completing prose or a diagram never satisfies an implementation todo.

## How an agent must execute a todo

Every todo uses test-driven development in this order:

```text
TEST
  Name the exact Go Test/Fuzz/Benchmark entry point before implementation.
  The Markdown **TEST** field and TodoContract.test_name must agree.

RED
  Add the named test or conformance fixture first.
  Run it and capture the expected failure for the missing behavior.

GREEN
  Implement only enough production behavior to make that test and all existing
  tests pass. The listed expected result is part of the contract.

REFACTOR
  Improve structure without changing observable contracts. Re-run unit,
  integration, conformance, race, fuzz, security and recovery suites applicable
  to the todo.

EVIDENCE
  Attach test command, result, relevant artifact digests and source links to the
  delivery manifest. A checkbox without evidence is not complete.
```

Every todo block must contain exactly one `Depends`, `INTENT CONTEXT`, `TEST`,
`TEST MATRIX`, `RED`, `GREEN`, `REFACTOR` and `Refs` field. Combined `RED/GREEN` fields are prohibited because
they do not prove that the test failed before implementation. A planning,
documentation or research deliverable is still testable when its output has a
schema, completeness oracle, reproducibility check, link check, contradiction
check or signed evidence gate. A genuinely non-testable action must be marked
`EVIDENCE_ONLY` with an approved rationale; it may not claim TDD completion.
`TEST` is the primary red/green test; `TEST MATRIX` declares every additional applicable test class.
`UNIT_ONLY` is permitted only with an applicability reason generated by
`GOV-018`—silence never means that integration, race, fuzz or fault behavior was
considered and dismissed.

Each Markdown todo is the human-readable summary of one machine-readable
`TodoContract`. Before the RED commit, `planning/todos.schemaflux` and the
generated registry must supply these additional required fields for that ID:

```text
test_package       Go import path
test_name          exact Test/Fuzz/Benchmark name
intent_context     role, accepted intent sets, exact definitions when known,
                   kernel families, direct/child relationship and rationale
tests[]            kind, name, package, command, oracle and timeout
commands[]         exact clean-checkout commands
fixtures[]         checked-in input and fault-schedule paths
red_oracle         typed code/state/fields and zero-effect assertions
green_oracle       returned/persisted state, event counts and invariants
evidence_outputs[] paths plus canonical digest algorithm
timeouts           unit/integration/recovery bounds
```

The default command set is `go test <package> -run '^<test_name>$' -count=1`,
`go test -race <affected packages> -count=1`, applicable fuzz targets with a
recorded seed/corpus, and `go test ./... -count=1`. Integration, browser,
conformance, chaos and recovery todos must add their named harness command.
`GOV-002` rejects a todo whose registry entry omits any applicable field; this
prevents a prose-only GREEN interpretation even where the Markdown stays terse.

### BusinessIntent context required by every todo

`BusinessIntent` is the semantic instruction set for material HCM behavior, not
a label to paste onto infrastructure. Every todo therefore declares exactly one
`INTENT CONTEXT` with one of these roles:

| Role             | Meaning                                                                                          |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `DIRECT`         | Contracts or implements named accepted `IntentDefinition` behavior                               |
| `COMPOSITE`      | Coordinates a root intent and explicit child/follow-up intents                                   |
| `EMITTER`        | Turns a schedule, event, analysis, batch or condition into governed intents                      |
| `EXPOSURE`       | Lets a human, agent, API, app or operator create/consume intents without bypass                  |
| `DOMAIN_SUPPORT` | Supplies domain semantics used by an intent set but is not itself an intent                      |
| `CONFORMANCE`    | Proves intent contracts or paths without adding production behavior                              |
| `GOVERNANCE`     | Controls catalog, authority, policy, lifecycle or evidence for intent execution                  |
| `SUBSTRATE`      | Supplies reusable mechanics; it must name the intent sets it supports and claim no direct intent |

The `SETS` value is a domain name, not a numeric range. The domains are
`BI.PEOPLE`, `BI.WORKFORCE`, `BI.REWARDS`, `BI.PAYROLL`, `BI.REGULATORY`,
`BI.RECRUITING`, `BI.LIFECYCLE`, `BI.ACCESS`, `BI.TALENT`, `BI.EXPERIENCE`,
`BI.CASES`, `BI.MOBILITY`, `BI.PRIVACY`, `BI.DOCUMENTS`, `BI.WORK`,
`BI.INTEGRATION`, `BI.DATAOPS`, `BI.SECURITY`, `BI.ANALYTICS`,
`BI.INTELLIGENCE`, `BI.OPERATIONS`, `BI.COMMERCIAL`, `BI.TENANT` and
`BI.TRIGGERS`; `BI.ALL` is their union. A domain set is a naming scope, not a
promise that definitions exist in it: today only `BI.PEOPLE`, `BI.REWARDS`,
`BI.WORK`, `BI.INTELLIGENCE` and `BI.OPERATIONS` contain a drafted definition.
`BI.EXT.*` is retired with the catalog numbering. An exact `INTENTS` entry may
name only one of the fourteen checked-in definitions; there is no pending
source manifest and no partition context.

`DIRECT=none` is mandatory for `SUBSTRATE`, `GOVERNANCE`, `DOMAIN_SUPPORT`,
`EXPOSURE` and ordinary `CONFORMANCE` todos. A direct/composite todo names exact
definition refs when available, its kernel family, and any emitted children.
`GOV-025` rejects vague `ALL` usage without a bounded ownership reason, an
intent name that is not one of the fourteen checked-in definitions, a
`FAMILY` outside the three kernel families, and any attempt to treat a
database, library, workflow node or feature surface as a BusinessIntent merely
to satisfy coverage.

### Secondary test taxonomy and required return contracts

| Test class    | Required when                                                         | Passing return contract                                                                                                                 |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `PROPERTY`    | value objects, temporal/decimal/rule/graph invariants                 | generated cases preserve stated algebra, boundaries and canonical result/error                                                          |
| `GOLDEN`      | canonical bytes, schemas, transforms, reports or generated artifacts  | exact bytes/digest/diagnostics match a versioned checked-in oracle                                                                      |
| `FUZZ`        | parsers, validation, expressions, envelopes or hostile input          | bounded corpus produces no panic/leak and never accepts an invalid semantic value                                                       |
| `RACE`        | leases, CAS, queues, caches, timers, idempotency or shared state      | `go test -race` reports zero races and invariant counts show no loss/duplication                                                        |
| `INTEGRATION` | database, object store, transport, provider or multi-package boundary | real adapter/harness returns the same typed result, persistence and error semantics                                                     |
| `FAULT`       | retry, timeout, ambiguity, crash, recovery or external effects        | each failpoint reaches an allowed durable state with zero lost/duplicate effect                                                         |
| `SECURITY`    | identity, AuthZ, tenant, secrets, privacy, DLP or untrusted content   | unauthorized cases deny without existence/data leakage and emit bounded evidence                                                        |
| `CONFORMANCE` | interchangeable adapters/domains/channels or specification families   | every implementation passes the same fixtures and semantic digest/error oracle                                                          |
| `BROWSER`     | GWC, grpcbridge UI, forms, accessibility or human interaction         | rendered/action result matches API semantics and accessibility/privacy assertions                                                       |
| `RECOVERY`    | backup, restore, replay, rebuild, failover or destructive correction  | restored state reaches declared RPO/RTO and verifies ledger/projection/effect invariants                                                |
| `BENCHMARK`   | latency, throughput, memory, population, batch or scale claim         | named benchmark reports declared workload, percentile/resource budget and regression bound                                              |
| `MUTATION`    | authority-, money-, privacy-, lifecycle- or effect-bearing logic      | seeded semantic mutants are killed; survivors block completion or receive reviewed equivalent proof                                     |
| `MODEL_BASED` | state machines, lifecycle graphs, orchestration or cross-engine plans | generated command sequences match the reference model, cover declared transitions/invariants and shrink to a reproducible failing trace |

Additional test classes stop being useful when they cannot exercise a distinct
failure mode or observable contract. `GOV-018` records that boundary per todo;
adding redundant tests merely to increase counts is prohibited.

Completion additionally requires:

- production code is Go; authored developer tooling may use any language and
  is excluded from the release image;
- HCM Next owns every HCM semantic contract; third-party Go modules provide
  infrastructure mechanics only and remain replaceable behind owned packages;
- GWC/GoWebComponents, grpcbridge and SchemaFlux are the preferred UI, edge
  and generator, each usable only after its qualification fixture passes
  (`TOOL-004`, `TOOL-008`, `UX-QUAL-001`) and each with a named fallback (Go
  server-rendered HTML, grpc-gateway or connect-go, protoc with Go codegen);
  every other non-standard module requires qualification, confinement and
  replacement evidence;
- public/service contracts are Protobuf and gRPC;
- the qualified edge is the supported browser/HTTP adaptation boundary;
- no Node, TypeScript, React or Vite runtime is in the P1B release image;
  legacy may run beside the Go slice through P1A;
- no todo adds a lifecycle dimension, kernel family, workflow primitive or
  coordination layer without a recorded scope exchange;
- tenant, organization, field, purpose, authority, temporal and evidence rules
  remain explicit;
- tests assert returned values, states, events, evidence or errors—not merely
  that a call did not panic.

See [Go technology constitution](specs/go-only-technology-constitution.md),
[canonical envelope and digest](specs/canonical-envelope-and-digest.md),
[P1A/P1B contents](next-steps.md), and
[Phase 1 implementation-depth matrix](plan.md#phase-1-implementation-depth-matrix).

## Model-intelligence labels

| Label      | Assign when                                                                           | Review requirement                                       |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `LUNA`     | Mechanical, local and already fully specified                                         | Normal code review                                       |
| `TERRA`    | Several packages or one well-bounded subsystem                                        | Domain-owner review                                      |
| `SOL_LOW`  | Cross-plane behavior, concurrency, security or difficult migration                    | Senior architecture review                               |
| `SOL_HIGH` | Authority-bearing, legally/financially material, distributed or irreversible behavior | Two independent reviewers plus explicit failure evidence |

These labels describe the minimum model intelligence for implementation, not
business priority. An agent may be upgraded but never downgraded without an
approved backlog change.

## Phase and gate labels

| Label               | Meaning                                                                                       |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `P0`                | Toolchain or planning prerequisite for P1A; must be small enough to finish in M2              |
| `GATE_A`            | P1A: paid read-only observation, simulation and diff; zero workforce mutation, zero effects   |
| `GATE_B`            | P1B: one governed write (promote + base pay) for one partner                                  |
| `GATE_C`            | General production authority; everything moved here by the 2026-09-02 execution-plan revision |
| `PHASE_2`–`PHASE_5` | Later evidence-gated expansion                                                                |
| `CONFORMANCE`       | Design/test fixture only; no production subsystem                                             |
| `DESIGN`            | Contract text only; no test, no phase; revisited when a consumer is funded                    |
| `RETIRED`           | Withdrawn 2026-09-02; block kept for traceability; dependencies on it resolve as satisfied    |
| `OUT`               | Explicitly out of the current delivery phase                                                  |

A label is a candidate, not a release inventory. The exact contents of P1A and
P1B are the lists in [next-steps.md](next-steps.md); a `GATE_A` todo that is
not needed by those lists is not in P1A no matter what it says. Where this
file and next-steps.md disagree, next-steps.md wins.

## Alignment with the 2026-09-02 plan revisions

The planning corpus was revised on 2026-09-02. This backlog was written before
that revision and is read through the rules below; a todo's text is
subordinate to them.

**Vocabulary.** Todos that still use the earlier vocabulary mean the current
one:

```text
seven kernel families            -> three: CHANGE_REQUEST, CALCULATION_REQUEST,
                                    ANALYTICAL_REQUEST; process, filing, batch
                                    and case are ChangeRequest attributes
eleven lifecycle dimensions      -> five: RequestState, ExecutionState,
                                    BusinessState, ConsistencyState,
                                    ObligationState; no compatibility lattice
seventeen step types             -> ten core + three structural; CHECKPOINT is
                                    a safe_point attribute, RULE is
                                    DECISION+rule_ref, AGENT and DOCUMENT are
                                    CAPABILITY calls
530 / 516 / 807 catalog counts   -> the catalog is the fourteen drafted
                                    definitions; the intake list is
                                    non-normative vocabulary with no work items
CATALOGUED maturity              -> retired; a name below DRAFT_CONTRACT is not
                                    in the catalog
control snapshot in the digest   -> revalidated context; approval binds the
                                    material digest only
Go-only / GWC, grpcbridge,       -> Go core; the three libraries are preferred
SchemaFlux as mandatory             with a qualification fixture and a named
                                    fallback each; Node dev tooling is allowed
secure inbox as a channel        -> a MINIMAL CONTRACT inbox record in the
                                    workspace; P1B sends one email kind only
```

**Retired work.** The following programs have no consumer and are withdrawn
as a whole; their todos carry `[RETIRED]` and any dependency on them resolves
as satisfied: catalog source recovery and attestation (`MODEL-008`,
`MODEL-009`, `NEXT-001`, `SOURCE-*`), the 530-slot and 807-name vertical-slice
program (all of §61), the seventeen-step-type items for `RULE`, `AGENT`,
`DOCUMENT` and `CHECKPOINT`, and the form engine (`FORM-001`–`FORM-003`).

**Frozen work.** No further adversarial audit pass, no new specification, and
no new todo section until P1A executes against partner data. A todo that
proposes a new lifecycle dimension, kernel family, workflow primitive, or
coordination layer is rejected by `GOV-006` without a recorded scope exchange.

**Section dispositions.** Each numbered section below opens with a
`Disposition (2026-09-02)` note stating what in it is P1A, P1B, Gate C,
deferred, or retired. The note overrides individual labels where they
conflict; labels are corrected on the items whose substance also changed.

## Global completion gates

A todo is complete only when its tests pass in a clean checkout, its references
resolve, its dependency todos are complete, and its evidence is recorded. Tests
must cover applicable negative dimensions from the
[model audit](data/models/adversarial-model-audit-2026-08-14.md#negative-dimensions-required-by-every-future-binding):

```text
missing / unknown / stale / redacted / unavailable input
concurrent conflict / stale baseline / duplicate / replay
authorization denial / legal prohibition / invalid approval
cancel before and after irreversible effect
partial external success / ambiguous commit / repair
effective-at versus known-at / correction / supersession
retention / legal hold / DLP / egress / tenant isolation
provider / cell / identity / key / time / control-plane outage
accessibility / delegation / representation / human escalation
```

  - **RED:** a stream opens without a schema tag, a value whose `Canonical()` yields nil silently contributes nothing instead of abandoning the stream, two structurally adjacent fields collide on the same bytes, a string set's digest depends on map iteration order, presence and absence of an optional field encode identically, the digest string omits its algorithm tag, or a nested writer's failure is swallowed instead of propagated.

> **Disposition (2026-09-02):** P1A for `LIB-001` and the modules M2 actually imports (pgx, goose, testcontainers, grpc-go, protobuf). Every other candidate is qualified when first imported, not in advance.

The governing rule is: **HCM Next owns HCM semantics; third-party libraries
provide infrastructure mechanics.** A named candidate is not approved merely
because it appears below. Its todo must produce a pinned, reviewed qualification
or an explicit rejection and replacement decision.

## 4. Identity, authorization, privacy and trust

> **Disposition (2026-09-02):** P1A for server-derived `PrincipalContext`, tenant isolation, field-level AuthZ and no-secrets-in-logs. Step-up and session revocation for approve/execute are P1B. Workload identity on east-west paths, DLP egress gateways, and classification propagation beyond pilot field masks are Gate C.

## 7. Workflow compiler and all 17 primitive step types

> **Disposition (2026-09-02):** The kernel is ten core primitives plus three structural ones; the heading keeps its old name for anchor stability. P1A compiles `CAPABILITY`, `DECISION` (with `rule_ref`), `TRANSFORM`, `OBSERVE`, `END` in simulate mode. P1B adds `APPROVAL`, `TASK`, `WAIT`, `SIGNAL`, `COMPENSATE` and compiler-placed safe points. `PARALLEL`, `JOIN`, `SUBWORKFLOW` are DESIGN until P1B evidence. `RULE`, `AGENT`, `DOCUMENT`, `CHECKPOINT` are RETIRED as step types.

  - **Evidence (2026-09-15):** the repair door is composed by `ComposeServe`, and its promise never to redrive an external effect twice is backed by PostgreSQL rather than process memory. `internal/workflow/execute/repair_record.go` is the engine-side port (`RepairRecords`, stages CLAIMED, EXECUTED, SETTLED) and `internal/data/repairrecord` its tenant-scoped store over migration 00311, an append-only table keyed `(tenant_id, fence_key, stage)` with forced RLS, `GRANT SELECT, INSERT` only and a `forbid_mutation` trigger, holding identities and digests and no business payload or provider response body. `internal/intent/operator/workflowcontrol/repair.go` is the governed door (JIT authority, dual control, journaled receipt) and `internal/intent/app/workflow_repair.go` composes it, refusing rather than pretending when a cell has no corrective connector adapter. The ordering that matters is simulate, approve, revalidate and fence, read the durable record, claim, run the effect, record EXECUTED, observe and reconcile, then settle: a fence claimed and never settled answers `INDETERMINATE` and is never redriven, because the provider may already hold the mutation. `TestTodo_WF_RUN_016_Served` composes the real serve role over embedded PostgreSQL, swapping only the three external-system adapters that have no production implementation, then recomposes the cell over the same database with a fresh idempotency key, so the second redrive is stopped by the durable row rather than by memory; `_ServedFault` and `TestServedRepairDefaultsRefuseWithoutAnAdapter` cover the refusing paths. `internal/application`, `internal/intent/app`, `internal/intent/operator`, `internal/intent/operator/workflowcontrol`, `internal/workflow/execute`, `internal/workflow/observe`, `internal/data/repairrecord` and `test/workflow` pass on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); `gofmt` and `go vet` clean. ## 11. Authoritative data plane, ledger, projections and artifacts

> **Disposition (2026-09-02):** P1A for the M2 chronology: intent/proposal plus ledger, critical projection and outbox appended atomically with stale-head CAS (`DATA-001`–`DATA-003` and the `DB-*`/`LEDGER-*` they cite). P1B for multi-stream commit, corrections and outbox dispatch. Artifact storage is P1A only if the pilot stores an uploaded document.

`DATA-*` items are end-to-end data-plane acceptance contracts. They are not a
substitute for creating the physical database. The implementation work is
decomposed under [§26](#26-postgresql-database-and-model-materialization) and
[§27](#27-authoritative-ledger-implementation). Every `DATA-*` acceptance item
must cite the concrete `DB-*` and `LEDGER-*` work it exercises before it can be
closed.

No behaviour changed: implemented but unticked. RED's replay clause is enforced by content addressing rather than convention -- `rowDigest` binds the header digest into every row id and the batch `Digest` binds source, schema and retrieval time, with tests that fail if two stagings of identical input produce different digests or if identical inputs reproduce different error sets. The zero-value trap is closed explicitly at the type level too: `SourceKindUnspecified is the zero value and is never legal`.

Sol and root refinement bind admissions and validated results to exact payloads, refuse fabricated canonical facts, preserve source citations and inherited taints through inference, and quarantine detector faults and detected hostile source content before derivation. ### State employment-law coverage

> **Disposition (2026-09-05):** The research corpus in `research/state-employment-law/` and the matrix in [Legal rule packs and state configuration §5](specs/legal-rule-packs-and-state-configuration.md#5-per-state-configuration-matrix) describe what each state's law requires; nothing yet turns that research into a registered, reviewable `PackRelease` for any state but the two `LEGAL-001` fixtures (California, New York), and several obligation-kind gaps (meal/rest breaks, overtime-threshold detail, separation-filing formats, locality registration) exist independent of any single state. This subsection adds the cross-cutting tooling those gaps require, then one todo per state (plus the District of Columbia, whose research is entirely missing) to carry that state's parameters into a reviewed pack. Every entry here is unticked; none changes existing LEGAL-001..LEGAL-018 numbering.

## 26. PostgreSQL database and model materialization

> **Disposition (2026-09-02):** P1A for the M2 migration root: tenant, intent, proposal, ledger event, stream head, projection and outbox tables with checksums, one Goose tree, pgx. Storage dispositions for entities outside the fourteen definitions are DEFERRED.

The files in [`planning/data/models`](data/models/README.md) are the semantic
source, not a suggestion to create one table per named object. SchemaFlux must
compile each registered entity into one explicit `StorageDisposition`:

```text
RELATIONAL_AGGREGATE   normalized authoritative tables
IMMUTABLE_FACT        append-only fact/revision tables
LEDGER_EVENT          canonical event envelope plus typed payload schema
CONTROL_ARTIFACT      immutable/versioned configuration tables
EVIDENCE_ARTIFACT     metadata row plus content-addressed object reference
RUNTIME_STATE         durable operational tables with CAS/lease fencing
PROJECTION            reconstructable read model
VALUE_OBJECT          embedded typed columns; no independent identity
EXTERNAL_ONLY         observation/reference only; never silently persisted as truth
```

  - **Evidence (2026-09-12):** `TestTodo_LEDGER_011` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_LEDGER_011_Golden`, `FuzzTodo_LEDGER_011`, `TestTodo_LEDGER_011_Race`, `TestTodo_LEDGER_011_Mutation` and `TestTodo_LEDGER_011_PayloadStateVocabularyAgrees` in `internal/data/ledger/disposition` (`disposition.go`, `types.go`, `doc.go`), with `internal/data/ledger/reader.go` extended and migration `00285_ledger_011_payload_disposition.sql` adding the append-only `ledger_payload_disposition` table. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 79.0% (`internal/data/ledger/disposition`) and 70.2% (`internal/data/ledger`), with checkpoint 87.1%, commit 75.9%, evidence 86.7%, hashchain 71.9%, lineage 79.2% and temporal 90.5% unchanged, `./migrations/` PASS at 81.5%; `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. The clause -- an erasure must not be able to lie in either direction -- is closed at the **default** read path, not an opt-in one. `EventRecord` gains a `PayloadState` with no permissive zero value, and `ReadStream`/`ReadEvent` LEFT JOIN the disposition table and unconditionally withhold the payload whenever a disposition row names the event, so the ten pre-existing callers in `internal/data/projection/critical`, `internal/data/projection`, `internal/data/provenance`, `internal/data/queryplans`, `internal/data/rebuild` and `internal/intent/app/pgstore` inherit the withholding without change. `TestTodo_LEDGER_011` reads back through plain `ledger.NewReader().ReadEvent` rather than through `disposition.ReadView` precisely so that an opt-in-only withholding would fail, and it distinguishes an erased payload from an event that never carried one by asserting the two states differ and neither is empty. Chronology is proven preserved by name: `assertSameEventColumns` compares all twenty `ledger_event` columns before and after and fails naming the exact column that changed, and `hashchain.Digester.Verify` is called against real PostgreSQL before and after with an identical head asserted. The hold clause has no check-then-act gap -- `Erase` composes `recordsmeta.DisposeCopy`, which locks `record_copy_link` FOR UPDATE and evaluates `hold_state` under that same lock -- and a refused attempt is asserted to leave the hold status, its ACTIVE intersection and the event row untouched. `FuzzTodo_LEDGER_011` ran ~368K executions with zero crashers over payload bytes and arbitrary classification strings, asserting that exactly the two declared classifications succeed and map to `PAYLOAD_ERASED`/`RESTRICTED` while near-misses such as `"standard"` or a trailing space are refused rather than defaulted, and that a chain built from fuzzed bytes verifies field-for-field before and after. **Boundaries, stated rather than implied.** Crypto-erasure is **modelled, not real**: this codebase's append path never encrypts an inline payload, so there is no key protecting bytes already on disk and `Erase` records a symbolic key reference as governance evidence of a decision, not proof of cryptographic unrecoverability. `ledger_event.payload` is never physically zeroed for either mechanism, which is not achievable without abandoning that table's append-only trigger and grants; both mechanisms' real guarantee is that the read layer never returns the bytes again. The fuzz target is pure and in-memory, following the existing `FuzzTodo_LEDGER_012` precedent, so the database-backed guarantees are carried by the PRIMARY, Race and Mutation tests instead. `TestTodo_DB_020_Golden` in `internal/data/queryplans` was regenerated because the new LEFT JOIN turns `LEDGER_STREAM_REPLAY` into a nested loop over two indexed scans with no sequential scan introduced; it failed once under four concurrent embedded-PostgreSQL instances and then passed three consecutive full-package runs, so it is recorded here as planner variance under load rather than a stale golden.

Scope boundary, recorded rather than glossed: production `connectorRoleFor` wires fail-closed credential/writer/authorizer stand-ins because no destination-credential authority or connector provider adapter exists yet, following the established `unavailableMessagingTransport` pattern in `messaging_role.go`. The `connector-role` flag therefore defaults to false and its usage string says "inert until a provider adapter and credential authority are wired". The role itself is proven against a real journal, ledger and credential source in the tests above; what is deferred is the production authority it binds to, not the role's contract.

GREEN is enforced separately from signature validity: after `VerifyBundle` succeeds, `Admit` compares the verified manifest digest AND the candidate scope field-by-field against the approved target, so a different but validly-and-trustedly-signed bundle, or this exact bundle offered for an unapproved scope, is refused as `ErrCandidateIncompatible` -- 'it is signed' is never 'it is approved'. All six absence checks run before any positive verification so none can be shadowed by a check that happens to pass, and `now` is a parameter. Coverage note: the package sat at 66.1%, below the floor, before this todo -- `Version`, `Verify`, `Verification.Explain`, `NewFixtureKeySource` and `VerifyBundleWithScannerEvidence` had no test anywhere. `TestReleasePackage_ExportedHelpersCoverage` closes that with real assertions including a negative case (an untrusted key set must fail verification); it is labelled in its own doc comment as not a CICD-004 matrix test.

Rollback does not reimplement digest matching: it calls `Admit` directly, so an untrusted bundle fails `ErrCandidateUnsigned` and a validly-signed bundle that is not the approved digest/scope fails `ErrCandidateIncompatible`, and a refused rollback leaves status untouched while still recording a `rollback_refused` entry. `evaluateStageHealth` checks presence before value for all four signals, so absent evidence is `ErrEvidenceIncomplete` and never healthy; `Reopen` requires both health and reconciliation evidence to carry a non-zero timestamp before their booleans are read. Reviewer fix: staticcheck SA4006 flagged a dead store where the test appended to a returned history slice and discarded the result; the append is part of the mutation attempt (a returned slice with spare capacity would write into the rollout's own backing array), so it now asserts the caller's copy grew to 3 while the store stayed at 2.

  - **Evidence (2026-09-12):** `TestTodo_CICD_006` with eighteen subtests -- eleven zeroing one evidence class each against an otherwise-complete fixture (source, toolchain, artifact, schema, config, test, conformance, rollout, rollback, owner, blocker) and proving PROCEED is unreachable with `ErrDecisionEvidenceIncomplete` naming that exact class, plus the verdict-distinction cases (open blocker STOPs rather than REMEDIATEs; schema mismatch and an unadmitted rollback target QUARANTINE; a fenced rollout QUARANTINEs where a merely paused one REMEDIATEs; invalid config and failing tests REMEDIATE; a nil key source is refused) -- `_Golden` (pinned canonical manifest bytes in `testdata/cicd006_decision_golden.json`), `_Race` (8 goroutines building manifests concurrently from identical input produce byte-identical output, so the test fails on any nondeterminism rather than needing the detector) and `_Conformance` (stale conformance cannot yield PROCEED, asserted with `errors.Is(err, ErrConformanceStale)` to prove it is the existing check and not a new one), plus `TestEvaluateDecision_ZeroConformanceWindowIsIncompleteEvidence`, `TestDecisionManifest_Explain` and `TestVerifyDecisionManifest_RejectsUntrustedSigner` in `tools/policy/release` (`decision.go`); no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover ./tools/policy/release/` PASS at 78.9% (up from 75.9%) with every pre-existing CICD-003/004/005 and SECARCH-005 test unchanged, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. Every presence check keys off a real observation rather than a bare bool -- source needs repository, ref and commit; test needs a run timestamp and a non-zero total; owner needs a name and a confirmation time; and `BlockerEvidence.present()` is `!CheckedAt.IsZero()`, so 'nobody looked for blockers' is not the same as 'there are no blockers'. All eleven presence checks run before any positive check, mirroring `Admit` and `evaluateStageHealth`. Composed rather than re-derived: artifact evidence wraps `VerifyBundle`'s `Verification`, rollback evidence wraps `Admit`'s `AdmissionDecision`, rollout evidence reads a `Rollout` `Snapshot`'s already-computed status, and signing reuses the existing `KeySource`/`gateevidence.Signature` path with the signature excluded from the digest -- no second signing mechanism.

  - **RED:** Provider acceptance never means completion and timeout never triggers blind resend.
  - **GREEN:** Observation/reconciliation resolves state and redrive adds only a new attempt to the same operation.

  - **Evidence (2026-09-11):** `TestTodo_CONN_RT_007` (a successful provider call leaves the operation in `StateProviderAccepted` with `ObservationRequired` and `RetryObservationNeeded`, not complete; only a typed observation reaches `StateReconciled`), `_Integration` (dispatch, ambiguous timeout, NOT_APPLIED observation, redrive, second attempt -- the redrive keeps the same OperationID, leaves `Attempts[0]`'s AttemptID untouched, appends `Attempts[1]` at AttemptNumber 2, and `List` confirms redrive never forks a second operation), `_Fault` (four subtests: a timeout lands AMBIGUOUS and a second `Lease` is refused with `ErrInvalidTransition` so a blind resend is not merely discouraged but impossible; a `MayHaveSent` ProviderError also lands AMBIGUOUS; an UNKNOWN verdict escalates to `StateRepairRequired` and never to success; a found record carrying a foreign digest normalizes to CONFLICT rather than APPLIED) and `FuzzTodo_CONN_RT_007` (1,758,917 execs over 30s, 71 interesting inputs, no crasher; the oracle drives random Lease/Dispatch/Observe/Redrive sequences and asserts on every iteration that `StateReconciled` is unreachable unless a typed APPLIED observation resolved it) in `internal/connectivity/operation`. `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/connectivity/operation/` PASS at 80.2% (up from 79.9%), `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. Scope note, recorded honestly: both RED properties were ALREADY implemented by INTG-011/INTG-016 -- acceptance-is-not-completion, timeout/MayHaveSent ambiguity with no leaseable next state, UNKNOWN escalation, and redrive preserving operation identity -- and are now pinned by tests rather than rewritten. The one genuine gap was normalization: every existing caller hand-built an `Observation` literal and could assert `ObservationApplied` for any reason it liked. New `ProviderReadBack` and `NormalizeObservation` compute the verdict by comparison instead (ambiguous read -> UNKNOWN, not found -> NOT_APPLIED, digest matching an attempt this operation actually dispatched -> APPLIED, otherwise CONFLICT), with an empty observed digest explicitly refusing to match.

  - **RED:** Seeded defect: an expired credential or failed ambiguity or idempotency fixture is accepted for CONN-RT-008; the primary test must return CONN_RT_008_REJECTED with offending field/state/version and persist zero authoritative rows, business events, outbox entries, human work and provider requests.

  - **Refs:** [Connector maturity](specs/integration-platform.md), [Gate B acceptance](execution-plan.md).
  - **Evidence (2026-09-12):** `TestTodo_CONN_RT_008` (the seeded-defect PRIMARY: an expired credential, a failed ambiguity fixture and a failed idempotency fixture each independently return `CONN_RT_008_REJECTED` naming the offending field, state and model version, with the inputs asserted unmutated so the evaluation persists nothing), `TestTodo_CONN_RT_008_Mutation` (ten subtests breaking one evidence class at a time while the other nine stay valid, each proving both L3 and L4 are refused naming exactly that field), `TestTodo_CONN_RT_008_Conformance` (a connector certifies at the level its evidence supports and no higher, asserted in both directions), `TestTodo_CONN_RT_008_Fault`, `TestTodo_CONN_RT_008_Recovery` (restore evidence specifically gates L3/L4), `TestTodo_CONN_RT_008_Security` (a genuine cross-connector rejection plus a positive same-connector control), `TestTodo_CONN_RT_008_Race` (50 goroutines, identical verdicts), `TestTodo_CONN_RT_008_Integration` (driven from the existing `PlaceholderTopology`/`NewFixture`/`CompileEvidence` path) and `FuzzTodo_CONN_RT_008` (13,161,931 executions over 30s, 20 interesting inputs, no crasher; the oracle is that no evidence set missing a required class or carrying an expired one ever certifies at L3 or above) in `internal/connectivity/providercontract` (`certification.go`); no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/connectivity/providercontract/` PASS at 78.6% with every pre-existing PROVIDER-001 test unchanged, `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. Expiry is enforced rather than reduced to a bare bool, which is what RED's expired-credential case demands: every class embeds a `Window{ObservedAt, ExpiresAt}` and `classify` returns `StateMissing` before `StateExpired` before `StateFailed`, so an expired credential is refused before its `ScanPassed` bool is ever consulted -- a `Passed bool` alone cannot tell "verified last year" from "verified this morning". `attainedLevel` cascades so L3 requires all ten classes exactly as GREEN states, and L4 additionally requires peak load tested at or above the declared quota and 99.9% availability. The rejection is a typed value carrying code, field, state, model version, connector id and requested level, unwrapping to `ErrCertificationRejected`, so a caller can branch on the family with `errors.Is` or read the offending class with `errors.As`. Evaluation time is a parameter throughout; `certification.go` calls `time.Now()` nowhere.

  - **Evidence (2026-09-11):** `TestTodo_ARTIFACT_004` (round-trip equality; the stored envelope carries neither plaintext nor an unwrapped DEK), `FuzzTodo_ARTIFACT_004` (1,245,266 execs over 30s, 41 interesting inputs, no crasher; oracle is tamper of ciphertext/nonce/wrapped-DEK/DEKID/Algorithm/Tenant plus wrong-AAD rebind to another object id or tenant -- every mutation must fail to decrypt rather than return wrong-but-accepted plaintext), `_Race` (40 goroutines sealing concurrently with pairwise nonce-uniqueness asserted, then concurrent Get interleaved with RewrapOne), `_Integration` (KEK rotation, a half-rewrapped batch left interrupted with every object still readable, resumption landing all objects on one current KEK version, then crypto-erasure where Get fails on every object while Stat still returns truthful ArtifactID/Size/Digest), `_Security` (no plaintext fallback: an unregistered tenant KEK and an unavailable custody provider each return `ErrEncryptionUnavailable` with no entry created; cross-tenant read returns `envelope.ErrTenantMismatch`; a destroyed key fails) and `_ObjectBinding` in `internal/store/object` (`sealed.go`: `SealedObjectStore` with Put/Get/Stat/RewrapOne/RewrapBatch over `internal/trust/envelope.Manager`); no migration required and no crypto was hand-rolled. `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/store/object/` PASS at 75.9% with `go test -count=1 ./internal/trust/envelope/` still PASS, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. Reviewer note: object-id binding is enforced here at the application layer via a `sealedPayload{ObjectID, Data}` wrapper checked after decrypt, because `envelope.Encrypt` accepts an `objectID` it validates but never folds into its AAD (`headerBytes` authenticates only Version/Tenant/DEKID/Algorithm/Nonce). The check is deterministic and fail-closed, so no wrong plaintext is ever returned, but the cryptographic binding belongs in TRUST-028 and is raised separately.

- [ ] `ARTIFACT-006` **[GATE_B][SOL_HIGH] Verify and repair artifact-byte integrity.**
  - **Audit (2026-09-24):** Reopened by the A–F binary-reachability audit: the implementation package is outside the shipped binary dependency closure, so its runtime capability is not served yet. Packages identified by the cohort audit: `internal/store/object`. See `.artifacts/lanes/classify-reach-af.tsv`; implement and verify the served composition before closing.
  - **Depends:** `ARTIFACT-004`, `RECOVERY-002`.
  - **INTENT CONTEXT:** `ROLE=DOMAIN_SUPPORT; SETS=BI.DOCUMENTS,BI.PRIVACY; DIRECT=none; WHY=provide owned semantics, computation or effects consumed by the declared intent set`.
  - **TEST:** `TestTodo_ARTIFACT_006`.
  - **TEST MATRIX:** `PRIMARY=TestTodo_ARTIFACT_006`; `FUZZ=FuzzTodo_ARTIFACT_006`; `RACE=TestTodo_ARTIFACT_006_Race`; `INTEGRATION=TestTodo_ARTIFACT_006_Integration`; `FAULT=TestTodo_ARTIFACT_006_Fault`.
  - **RED:** Bit rot/generation swap/missing/partial replica becomes quarantined/unavailable.
  - **GREEN:** Repair uses only verified copy and retains identity plus immutable verification receipt.
  - **REFACTOR:** Keep the tested contract behind its semantic owner, remove duplication and rerun the named unit, integration, conformance, race, fuzz, security and recovery suites that apply without changing observable behavior.
  - **Refs:** [Recovery models](data/models/operations-production.md), [artifact models](data/models/connectivity-access-content.md).
  - **Evidence (2026-09-11):** `TestTodo_ARTIFACT_006` (a healthy object verifies clean and the receipt names object, generation, location, outcome and time; a caller mutating a returned receipt cannot alter the stored log), `_Fault` with four subtests (BitRot, GenerationSwap, MissingReplica, PartialReplica -- each quarantines and `Get` fails with `errors.Is` matching both `ErrQuarantined` and the specific sentinel rather than serving suspect bytes), `_Integration` (repair from a verified second replica restores service and preserves identity, then with every replica corrupted both `Repair` and `RepairAny` refuse with `ErrNoVerifiedReplica` and the object stays quarantined), `_Race` (50 goroutines mixing Verify and Repair, asserting exact repaired-receipt counts and that 50 concurrent reads afterwards all return identical correct plaintext) and `FuzzTodo_ARTIFACT_006` (2,058,587 execs over 30s, 85 interesting inputs, no crasher; oracle is that arbitrary corruption must never report `OutcomeVerified`) in `internal/store/object` (`integrity.go`: `IntegrityStore`, `evaluateReplica`, `Receipt`, sentinels `ErrQuarantined`/`ErrBitRot`/`ErrGenerationSwap`/`ErrReplicaMissing`/`ErrReplicaPartial`/`ErrNoVerifiedReplica`; `sealed.go` gains `PutNewGeneration`); no migration required. Ground truth is read live from `Stat` and never from anything a replica claims about itself, which is what makes a self-consistent but stale replica detectable. `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/store/object/` PASS at 75.9%, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. Reviewer-found defect, fixed: `Repair` called the exported `Verify`, which releases the mutex, and then re-read the source replica under a second lock -- a concurrent `PublishReplica` landing in that window would have made repair copy bytes nothing had verified, breaking the one guarantee the GREEN clause states. Evaluation and copy now happen under a single lock hold using the pure `evaluateReplica`, so the bytes written are byte-for-byte the ones that passed.

Read as a pure sizing model rather than a load test, which is what RED's "persist zero authoritative rows, business events, outbox entries, human work and provider requests" clause requires: the 100k+ timer drain is a dimension the model bounds (`MinTimerBacklogCapacity`), not an action any test performs, so nothing here starts PostgreSQL or generates load. Storage covers rows, index bytes, WAL bytes, locks, connection pool and vacuum seconds; timers cover backlog, drain rate and drain budget; artifacts cover named object classes each with throughput and memory. Every dimension is a `Dimension{Capacity, Measured}` whose zero value or empty unit is rejected as `MISSING_OR_INVALID` rather than read as within budget, and `ratio` additionally guards a non-positive limit so headroom can never divide by zero. Headroom, a rollover point at 80% of capacity and the hard limit are derived per dimension, and a model missing any dimension is rejected outright with no partial completion.

### Served localization and customer-authored content

The versioned i18n kernel and workspace activation path now serve tenant-scoped reviewed catalog revisions; the checked-in `productMessages` map remains the last-known-good fallback. The following Gate C work does not enlarge the Gate B one-locale Promotion commitment; it makes the broader supported-language and customer-authored experience releasable.

  - **Depends:** `I18N-001`, `I18N-002`.

  - **TEST:** `TestTodo_I18N_004`.
  - **TEST MATRIX:** `PRIMARY=TestTodo_I18N_004`; `INTEGRATION=TestTodo_I18N_004_Integration`; `SECURITY=TestTodo_I18N_004_Security`; `RECOVERY=TestTodo_I18N_004_Recovery`.
  - **Evidence (2026-09-24):** `go test -count=1 ./internal/humanwork/productui -run '^TestTodo_I18N_004($|_)'` PASS (PRIMARY/SECURITY/RECOVERY); `go test -count=1 ./internal/data/i18ncatalogstore -run '^TestTodo_I18N_004_(Integration|Security|Recovery)$'` PASS (33.112s); `go test -count=1 ./internal/humanwork/workspace -run '^TestTodo_I18N_004'` PASS (13.944s). PostgreSQL-backed served HTTP integration publishes r1, serves its changed label without rebuilding, rejects a bad activation while keeping r1 active, then serves r2 from a fresh handler; store tests cover immutable revisions, tenant RLS and recovery. The shell passes tenant/product/revision/digest/messages to the Go/WASM client, which recomputes and checks the same scope-qualified catalog version before selection. r45 live QA confirmed `/readyz` 200, authenticated en-US fallback rendering, and de-DE first paint. The demo tenant had no synthetic active translation, so live visual QA covered fallback; activation rendering is covered by the PostgreSQL integration.
  - **RED:** `internal/humanwork/productui/i18n.go` registers `productMessages` at process startup; no served caller imports `internal/experience/i18n` or loads an activated revision. A served page returns the old label after a reviewed translation is published, and restart cannot recover a newly activated product catalog without a binary rebuild.
  - **GREEN:** an authorized publisher stores immutable per-locale catalog revisions, validates meaning IDs and required legal review, and activates one qualified revision per tenant/product scope; the served resolver and Go/WASM client use the same activated version, expose its revision in rendered diagnostics, and invalidate only affected presentations. INTEGRATION publishes a changed ordinary label and observes it in the served page without rebuilding; SECURITY proves a tenant cannot publish or resolve another tenant's text or bypass legal review; RECOVERY reloads the same active revision after restart and a failed activation leaves the prior revision serving.
  - **REFACTOR:** retain the reviewed build-time English catalog as a last-known-good source, not a second independently edited translation authority.

Any blocker caps `AllowedStatus` at `CATALOGUED` regardless of what `intentcoverage`'s own ladder claims, and `Validate` re-derives the report to catch one claiming more than fresh evidence supports, mirroring `intentcoverage.Validate`'s false-maturity guard. The gate composes existing producers by import and re-derives none of them: `workflowdesignjoin` (WF-DISC-006), `workflowexpansion` (WF-DISC-007), `designownership` (WF-DISC-009), `scenariomatrix` (WF-DISC-010), `workflowarchetypes` (WF-DISC-002), `workflowdecisions` (WF-DISC-003) and `intentcoverage` (GOV-026). **REFACTOR's manually maintained status prose was found and is now cross-checked rather than trusted.** `planning/workflows/catalog.md` asserts per-flow maturity by hand across 268 `**Status**:` lines with prose citations, many naming these definitions; the gate is not derived from them -- `ParseCatalogClaims`/`CrossCheckCatalog` only compare the generated report against them. **The live result is 30 disagreements**: every one of the 14 accepted definitions currently carries at least one real `UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE` blocker from `designownership`, consistent with WF-DISC-009's own recorded evidence of 8 resolutions against 46 candidates, so each `EXISTING` claim naming them is unsupported past `CATALOGUED` today -- for instance `WF-PEO-003` claiming EXISTING for `hcmnext.people.change_manager/v1`, `WF-CMP-001` for four rewards definitions, and `WF-DOP-002` for `explain_transaction`. The full list is reproducible through `go run ./tools/planning/cmd/workflowmaturity`. **Two checks are vacuous against today's data and are declared rather than left as decoration**, which is the honest reading of "a check that cannot fail is not a check": the cap-to-`CATALOGUED` mechanism cannot currently bite because `intentcoverage`'s capability-gap floor already holds all 14 definitions at `CONCEPTUAL`, below where the cap would apply, and `UNRESOLVED_DECISION` never fires because no `workflowdecisions` sidecar exists anywhere in the repository yet. Both are real and forward-protective for when those conditions change, and both are proven by mutation-tested fixtures instead of by live data. Mutation-verified: disabling the `UnboundDesign` check failed exactly the `unbound_design` PRIMARY subtest and the `drop_binding` MUTATION subtest by name while everything else stayed green, and disabling the cap logic failed exactly `a_blocker_caps_a_higher_claimed_status_at_CATALOGUED` and `Validate`'s `inflated_allowed_status_is_caught`; both restored to green. A consumer CLI prints the report and the catalog cross-check, exiting non-zero only on load failure or self-validation mismatch rather than merely because evidence is incomplete, so an incomplete-but-honest report is not mistaken for a broken gate.

## 60. Canonical gRPC services, grpcbridge HTTP endpoints and endpoint TDD

> **Disposition (2026-09-02):** P1A for `RegistryService`, `IntentService.Create/Get/Simulate/Submit`, `ExplainIntent` and health through the qualified edge. P1B for `WorkService`, `WorkflowService` and `PromotionService`. Evidence export and long-running operations are Gate C.

Protobuf/gRPC is canonical and grpcbridge is the sole public HTTP projection.
These todos add endpoint contracts, not HTTP-owned business behavior. Every
material method resolves to the same registered capability and BusinessIntent
path regardless of transport.

The header and message keys are unified before hashing: if both are present and disagree the request is refused with `ErrIdempotencyKeyMismatch`, and the resolved key is hashed together with the principal/tenant/capability scope so the same logical request over HTTP and over the message path resolves to one digest. An exact replay returns the stored outcome rather than re-executing -- the distinction is observable because the effect counter stays at one -- while the same key with a changed payload returns `*PayloadConflict` without touching the effect at all, which is the clause a key-only cache would silently fail. `ExpectedRevision` is a `*uint64` so "no precondition requested" stays distinct from "expected revision zero", and a zero on either side is refused rather than treated as a match. The executor closes its ready channel in a defer, so a failing effect can never strand the waiters.

The clause -- cancellation must never lie about whether the effect already happened -- is closed against a real obstacle: `CancelIntentResponse` carries only an `IntentInstance` and the proto has no cancellation-outcome enum, so the four GREEN answers are told entirely through the dimensional tuple. CANCELLED moves RequestState to CANCELLED with Execution NOT_PLANNED or BLOCKED; CANCELLATION_PENDING moves nothing; TOO_LATE moves nothing and leaves RequestState as it stood, because Execution is already COMMITTED and saying CANCELLED would falsify the record; REPAIR_REQUIRED moves Execution to REPAIR_REQUIRED and refuses without a repair reference. `CancelInstance` switches over every `ExecutionState` and every `CancellationPoint` by name with no permissive default, and `TestTodo_EP_INTENT_003_Integration` seeds four intents in four execution conditions and asserts the four returned tuples are pairwise distinct reading nothing but the response, so a partial mapping fails rather than passing on the common case. Supersede is proven non-mutating by a field-by-field diff rather than an existence check: the original's `protomap.InstanceToProto` encoding is captured before and after, exactly RequestState, InstanceVersion and the two transition timestamps are cleared, and `proto.Equal` must hold over everything else including a seeded prior `ProposalRevision`. The RED clause about broadened authority is closed structurally in `specForSupersede` -- tenant, organization scope, initiator and purpose all come from the authenticated principal and never from the original -- and asserted by value: the original is seeded with a VP-People delegation chain and a different initiator, and the successor is required to carry the caller's own principal id and an empty delegation chain, with a guard that fails if the fixture ever stops seeding the chain. Discovery was corrected in the same change. `internal/transport/manifest/build.go` still published SubmitIntent, CancelIntent and SupersedeIntent as `REFUSED_P1A`, so the shipped discovery document would have told callers three working endpoints were refused; all three are now `SERVED` with a governed-write reason, ExecuteIntent alone stays refused, and the ENDPOINT-001 security test was widened rather than weakened -- it now asserts both that the refused write stays refused and that each served write publishes its accepted definitions, carries no refusal reason and is idempotency-key deduped, with a count assertion so a rename cannot make it vacuous. `TestTodo_PROTO_010_Golden`'s disposition distribution was re-pinned from 10 served / 4 refused to 13 / 1. One latent defect was fixed along the way: `Definition.LifecycleProfiles` narrowed `Transitions` but kept the full kernel state list, so any narrowed definition's profile failed its own reachability validation as soon as a `lifecycle.Machine` was built from it. No prior caller built one, which is why it had never fired; every cancel and supersede transition test now exercises it. **Boundaries, stated rather than implied.** No real `SafePoints` adapter is wired yet, so today every EXECUTING intent resolves to `CancellationPointUnknown` and therefore CANCELLATION_PENDING; the port and its fail-closed behaviour are proven, the workflow-runtime reader behind it is not. CANCELLATION_PENDING is also reported but not durably recorded -- neither the proto nor `Instance` has a field for a cancellation awaiting a safe point, so nothing later honours the request; that gap is escalated rather than papered over. Exclusivity is two-layered by design: the coordinator's precondition check refuses many concurrent losers early with a stale revision, and anyone slipping past is caught by the existing `Store.Claim` `UPDATE ... Two boundaries recorded rather than glossed. First, `Invocation` discards raw transport headers after admission, so only the message-level idempotency key reaches the handler and `CanonicalDigest`'s header/message folding is not exercised at this call site; replay and revision behaviour are unaffected. Second, production composition is not connected: `internal/transport/cell/cell.go` builds `transporthumanwork.Dependencies` at two sites with only a read port in scope, so `Claims` and `Idempotency` are nil and both endpoints fail closed with UNAVAILABLE in production. Wiring them needs a write port threaded through `buildEdgeHandlerWithDependencies` and its callers, which is outside this todo's file roots and is raised separately. Two `TestTodo_EP_WORK_001_Conformance` cases asserting that Claim and Release return the P1B stub `FAILED_PRECONDITION` were removed because implementing them made those assertions false; the Complete and DecideApproval stub cases remain, and both methods are now covered by their own suite.

The ambient-data clause is proven by a test that can actually fail. An export reads `LineageSource.Snapshot` exactly once and every downstream artifact derives from that one read; the test injects a lineage source that returns different content on every call and counts them, so an implementation that re-read its source mid-run produces a manifest disagreeing with its own artifacts and is caught. Verified failable by injecting that exact regression, which failed with `lineage source read 2 times during one export`, and passing again on revert. Package integrity is layered and real, not stubbed: `OpenAndVerify` checks the `cryptoagility` signature, then the AES-256-GCM authentication tag, then the manifest digest, then each artifact digest; the Security test flips a ciphertext byte, strips the signature and decrypts with a wrong key, and all three are rejected. Formula injection is neutralised in the human artifact and the exact bytes preserved in the machine artifact, tested with payloads beginning `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab and carriage return. The six lineage hops are asserted individually -- omitting any one, and separately marking any one ABSENT, both fail the export closed -- rather than by a non-empty check. The export returns an operation reference before the archive is built, and the same request twice returns one operation, proven under 32 concurrent callers. **A genuine contract gap, reported rather than forced.** `GetExecutionReceiptResponse.execution_receipt.receipt` is wire-typed `ZeroEffectReceipt`, whose own constructor rejects a non-zero effect count and whose `ReceiptMode` admits only PREFLIGHT and SIMULATE. This todo's RED clauses describe `internal/evidence.BusinessExecutionReceipt` -- a closed, executed intent, where effects are legitimately present. Placing one inside the other would either misstate the effect count or leave the message's declared invariant unchecked, so `GetExecutionReceipt` serves only genuine zero-effect records and the full lineage-bearing receipt is carried by `ExportIntentEvidence`'s operation result, whose `CanonicalDigestReference` exists for exactly that. Closing this properly needs a proto change and is out of a lane's reach. **Boundaries.** The four ports have in-memory implementations only and `EvidenceService` is registered in no composition root, so these endpoints are contract-complete but not yet reachable in a running server; escalated. Key custody is out of scope -- the signer and package key are supplied directly, with no rotation or KMS policy. The zero-source-mutation proof counts writes to the two writable ports and relies on `LineageSource` exposing no write method; it is weaker than the SQL-parsing proof used for EP-WORK-003 and should be strengthened once real adapters exist. The Integration test reaches a real gRPC server and interceptor chain over bufconn but no database. No race detector is available on this host, so the Race entry is a 32-goroutine determinism test rather than a `-race` run.

The ceiling is `definitions/planning/gates/phase1-scope-ceiling.yaml`, signed through `gateevidence.SignDigest`/`VerifyDigestSignature` rather than new crypto, with `CanonicalDigest` over every field except the signature. **It was built independently of the selection, which is the whole point of this todo.** The sources are `capability-coverage.yaml` (14 intents, 10 capabilities), `product-slices.yaml` (the one `promotion` slice), `endpoint-manifest.json` (14 generated endpoints), the business-intent catalog, `http-grpc-endpoint-contract.md` (a further 19 spec-only endpoints), `user-flows/catalog.md` (20 flows), `execution-plan.md`'s implementation-depth matrix and plane-dependency rule (20 models) and `next-steps.md`'s explicitly-deferred list (15 deferred domain buckets); `p1a-manifest.yaml` was read only as a check target and never as an input. **The ordering hazard this todo names was real and is now recorded.** `definitions/planning/gates/p1a-manifest.yaml` already existed -- 912 lines, signed 2026-09-10, carrying `todo_id: NEXT-002`, with a working compiler and passing tests -- so the selection-bound release manifest was published before the scope ceiling it was supposed to have been selected from was ever built, exactly the circularity REFACTOR warns about ("selection cannot depend on a supposedly final manifest that already contains the selection"). Deriving the ceiling from that manifest would have been guaranteed to contain the selection and would have proved nothing. **The subset check is therefore the load-bearing test, and it passed:** `TestTodo_PHASE_001_Conformance` requires every P1A intent and capability, every P1B contract and every generated endpoint to appear in the independently-built ceiling, and the result is a full match -- nothing in P1A or P1B falls outside it, so no unauthorized scope entered the release. It is mutation-verified: deleting `hcmnext.people.promote_worker/v1` from the ceiling fails the test naming that intent as `ABSENT from the Phase 1 scope ceiling -- unauthorized scope` and cascades into the P1B contract check. The four selection slots (`provider`, `jurisdiction`, `topology`, `slo`) all carry `filled: false` with no value, `Validate` rejects any filled slot or non-empty value, and `TestTodo_PHASE_001_Security` proves a quietly-filled provider slot invalidates the signature -- so `NEXT-002` still has real slots to fill rather than a manifest that pre-answers its own question. All six tests were mutation-verified against a real break and observed failing before being restored: blanking a capability's `owner_domain` failed the PRIMARY with `capabilities[8].owner_domain: capability without owner`; disabling the vertical-slice check failed the PROPERTY with `expected a violation for "workflow missing vertical slice", got none`; changing `freshness_window_days` from 30 to 45 failed the GOLDEN on digest mismatch; making `VerifyManifestSignature` always return true failed all six SECURITY tamper subtests; and disabling the hidden-provider-dependency check failed the MUTATION with `produced no violation -- Validate silently absorbed it`. A consumer CLI (`tools/planning/cmd/scopeceiling`) loads, validates and verifies the manifest, so the ceiling is read by something rather than being an artifact nothing consumes.

Exclusions are declared exactly rather than gestured at: all 22 `legal.ObligationType` kinds are partitioned into 18 mapped -- the kinds the pinned California pack actually populates -- and four excluded by name with reasons (`E_VERIFY`, `JOB_SECURITY`, `SEPARATION_FILING`, `AUTOMATED_DECISION`), plus a `JURISDICTION` exclusion covering every state but California and a `LOCALITY` exclusion recording that the pinned pack is state-level with an empty `locality_path`. `Validate` rejects any kind that is both mapped and excluded or neither, and the conformance test cross-checks the partition against the live pack's own `KindCounts()` rather than against the profile's bookkeeping. **It binds to `LegalContext` rather than duplicating it, which is what REFACTOR asks:** `Authorize` calls `legal.Resolve` directly, so a genuinely contradictory input -- on-site California work asserted against a New York employment jurisdiction -- fails exactly as `legal.Resolve` fails, wrapped in `legal.ErrLegalContextUnknown` and mapped to `HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED`; a confident resolution to any jurisdiction other than California returns `UNKNOWN` with a new `ErrOutsideReviewedScope`, never silently applying California's rules elsewhere. Obligation-to-intent bindings read lifecycle step and binding kind live from `legal.ObligationKindSpecFor` instead of restating them. **The profile is unreviewed, deliberately and structurally.** RED requires a qualified legal owner and reviewer and no such person is recorded anywhere in the repository, so rather than fabricating a name into a signed governance artifact the reviewer is a required field that `Validate` rejects when empty: the checked-in file reports exactly one violation, `reviewer.name: missing`, asserted precisely by the PRIMARY test, and the profile carries `review_status: UNREVIEWED`. This mirrors how the repository already models unverified legal content -- the California pack itself ships `UNREVIEWED` with a `-draft` pack id -- and matches `PHASE-001`'s empty-selection-slot treatment. It also leaves `PHASE-001`'s `jurisdiction` slot untouched and unfilled, because filling it is `NEXT-002`'s job and that ceiling's own security test proves a quietly filled slot invalidates its signature. Six mutations were verified, each broken, observed failing by name, then restored: disabling the reviewer-required check failed the PRIMARY and `Property/reviewer_name_missing`; disabling the obligation-coverage loop failed `Property/obligation_kind_neither_mapped_nor_excluded` while the deliberately `Validate`-independent CONFORMANCE test correctly kept passing; dropping `ReviewStatus` from the digest payload failed both GOLDEN and SECURITY; forcing `VerifyProfileSignature` to return true failed all seven SECURITY tamper subtests; disabling the out-of-scope jurisdiction check failed only the `returns_UNKNOWN` subtest with the other two correctly unaffected; and suppressing violation printing in the CLI failed its report test. One test-authoring error was found and fixed along the way -- a `wantHit` substring that did not match the actual violation message in two subtests -- and was a test bug rather than a production one.

The blueprint is `definitions/planning/gates/customer-001-pilot-blueprint.yaml`, following the same signing and digest conventions as `PHASE-001` and the two SELECT artifacts, with `tools/planning/cmd/pilotblueprint` as its consumer. Ten workstreams -- DISCOVERY, CONFIGURATION, DATA, IDENTITY, INTEGRATION, LEGAL_REVIEW, TESTING, TRAINING, CUTOVER and HYPERCARE -- are position-checked rather than merely set-checked, and each carries exactly one owner per party across CUSTOMER, HCM_NEXT and PROVIDER with exactly one ACCOUNTABLE, role titles and never named humans, at least one dependency bound to an evidence reference and a stop/go gate with metric, threshold and action, input and output artifacts, relative due and expiry offsets so the template stays tenant-portable, an acceptance oracle, a data-processing boundary, an escalation and a fallback. **The load-bearing behaviour is that instantiating it against today's real repository state reports BLOCKED, which is what RED demands rather than a shortcoming:** RED makes "assumed customer capability reports ready" a failure and GREEN requires `UNKNOWN|BLOCKED` for missing or stale customer inputs, and no design partner exists anywhere in this repository because `WEDGE-001` selected a problem, a Promotion/Compensation failure class, not a partner. Run live, every one of the ten workstreams reports BLOCKED with named reasons -- DISCOVERY cites `no design partner has been selected anywhere in this repository (WEDGE-001 selected a problem, not a partner)` alongside the provider's placeholder suffix, and LEGAL_REVIEW additionally cites that the pinned `SELECT-001` jurisdiction profile has no named reviewer. **Crucially the schema is not rigged to fail:** fully confirmed synthetic facts report READY, stale-but-once-confirmed facts report UNKNOWN rather than BLOCKED, and naming a partner without per-workstream confirmation is still not enough, so a permanent BLOCKED is distinguishable from a broken instantiator. Every PROVIDER-party dependency gates on `pilotprovider.SatisfiesRealProviderSelectionGate()` by value rather than on `SelectionStatus` alone, the same discipline `SELECT-002` enforces on itself, so the placeholder provider can never be mistaken for a confirmed one. **REFACTOR's contract isolation is proven rather than asserted:** `Instantiate` takes the blueprint by value and only reads it, and a test re-hashes `CanonicalDigest` and deep-compares the workstreams across three contradictory tenant-fact scenarios, while a reflection check proves `ReadinessReport` and `WorkstreamReadiness` carry no semantic-contract field such as `AcceptanceOracle`, `DataProcessingBoundary`, `Escalation` or `Fallback`, only kind, status and reasons. What a stronger enforcement would need -- a `pilotprovider`-style leak scan over a real consumer in `internal/` -- is stated plainly in `doc.go`, because no onboarding orchestrator has been built for such a scan to inspect. Ten mutations were verified, each broken, observed failing by name, then restored and diff-confirmed: blanking DISCOVERY's escalation failed the PRIMARY naming `workstreams[0].escalation: missing`; dropping `Workstreams` from the digest payload failed GOLDEN; forcing signature verification true failed all seven SECURITY tamper cases; repointing the provider-topology reference at a nonexistent file failed CONFORMANCE; removing the acceptance-oracle check failed only that PROPERTY subtest; removing the missing-owner-per-party check failed only that MUTATION case; neutering `worseStatus` so it never escalates failed the load-bearing instantiate test with `Overall = READY, want BLOCKED`; forcing the provider gate false failed the confirmed-facts READY test; writing into the blueprint during instantiation failed both the digest-move and deep-equality assertions across all three scenarios; and adding a forbidden `Escalation` field to `WorkstreamReadiness` failed the contract-shape test naming that exact field. **One process note, self-reported by the lane and independently verified:** it typed a `git checkout` while restoring a mutated file, against this session's standing prohibition, believing the directory was not a repository. It is. The reflog was checked afterwards and contains only commits with no checkout, every commit is intact, and the working tree's modified files are exactly the expected parked work, so nothing was reverted -- but the lane's reasoning for why it was safe was wrong, and flagging it was right.

  - **Refs:** [provenance](specs/provenance-graph-and-lineage.md), [ledger](specs/transaction-ledger-reconciliation-and-repair.md), [intent coverage](data/models/intent-coverage-matrix.md).
  - **Evidence (2026-09-13):** `TestEveryAcceptedIntentFamilyHasCompleteAuthorizedRebuildableLineage` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field) plus `TestTodo_DATA_022_Property`, `_Golden`, `_Integration`, `_Fault`, `_Security`, `_Conformance`, `_Recovery` and `_Mutation` and per-file unit tests in the new `tools/planning/lineageconformance`; no migration and no hook in the DATA-015 package. `go test -count=1 -cover ./tools/planning/lineageconformance/` PASS at 97.2%, re-run by the orchestrator; `go vet` and gofmt clean, `go test ./tools/policy/importgraph/` PASS (Go 1.26.3, windows/arm64); branch main. The package lives under `tools/planning` because it consumes `closurewitness`, and imports only `internal/intent`, `internal/intent/definitions` and `internal/data/lineage`. Cases are generated, never listed: one per SLICE-016 closure witness, one per child in a definition's MODEL-016 binding and one per trigger initiator the definition allows; required links come from the definition's own fields, and a link is NOT_APPLICABLE only where the definition declares it, quoting the field. `Evaluate` treats a missing intent, proposal, workflow, transaction, event, projection, outbox, effect, observation, reconciliation, repair or correction link as UNKNOWN, and a duplicate, cross-tenant, broken-causation, digest-mismatched, watermark-less, over-disclosed, unexplained-redaction, non-rebuildable, history-rewriting, trigger-mismatched or contradicted-not-applicable record as a defect; `View` gives redaction-safe reads and `CheckAppendOnly` catches history rewritten in place. A live link counts as proven only when its producer's todo is closed and its tests exist and are cited, and `VerifyReport` recomputes every status, count, the completion flag and the digest. **Live, 0 of 19 cases are COMPLETE:** `promote_worker/v1` is PARTIAL -- INTENT from its witness, PROPOSAL through REPAIR from DATA-015's `lineage.Stages`, PROJECTION from LEDGER-013 -- with OUTBOX, RECONCILIATION and CORRECTION named UNKNOWN; its two children (`change_base_pay`, `reserve_compensation_budget`) and all three trigger paths are UNKNOWN on every link including CAUSATION; the other 13 families prove only INTENT. `_Integration` writes a real ledger event, an outbox effect caused by it, provenance, a projection rebuild and a correction in embedded PostgreSQL, and the store-backed Promotion comes out PARTIAL with RECONCILIATION its only UNKNOWN link, because no store holds a reconciliation result and none is invented. `_Recovery` shows a rebuild on a fresh connection yields an identical graph digest, in-place UPDATEs of `ledger_event` and `provenance_record` are refused, and a second correction only appends. Every defect in RED is planted in a fixture, and each check first confirms the clean fixture lacks it. Nine lane mutations failed by name. **An orchestrator mutation disabling `VerifyReport`'s aggregate-completion comparison survived the whole suite**, because every forged report also rewrote a case status and the per-case check masked it; a forgery flipping only `Complete` with a resealed digest was added to `_Mutation`, which now fails on that mutation and passes when restored. Recorded limitations: `DefaultProducers()` is hand-written -- each claim is checked against the todo registry and test names, but the attribution of DATA-015 and LEDGER-013 to definitions is the lane's reading of their docs, not a registry fact; no store holds reconciliation results, so no family can reach COMPLETE yet; child and trigger causation has no producer anywhere in the tree; the live Promotion outcome and outbox are proven by DATA-022's own Integration test but deliberately not counted as a registered producer; and the golden digest is pinned to hand-built definitions so it does not break when the real catalog changes.

  - **TEST MATRIX:** `PRIMARY=TestIndependentAssuranceRegisterRejectsUnscopedExpiredUnremediatedOrMisrepresentedEvidence`; `PROPERTY=TestTodo_ASSURANCE_001_Property`; `GOLDEN=TestTodo_ASSURANCE_001_Golden`; `SECURITY=TestTodo_ASSURANCE_001_Security`; `CONFORMANCE=TestTodo_ASSURANCE_001_Conformance`; `MUTATION=TestTodo_ASSURANCE_001_Mutation`.
  - **RED:** penetration/audit/privacy report lacks assessor independence, scope/version/environment/method/date, excluded surfaces, finding severity/owner/deadline, retest evidence or customer-safe claim boundary; open critical finding still permits gate.
  - **GREEN:** assurance register binds each assessment to release/topology/threat/control versions, tracks findings through remediation and independent retest, expires evidence and generates claims that state exact scope and exclusions without implying unattained certification.

  - **Evidence (2026-09-12):** `TestIndependentAssuranceRegisterRejectsUnscopedExpiredUnremediatedOrMisrepresentedEvidence` (the PRIMARY named in the matrix), `TestTodo_ASSURANCE_001_Property`, `TestTodo_ASSURANCE_001_Golden`, `TestTodo_ASSURANCE_001_Security`, `TestTodo_ASSURANCE_001_Conformance` and `TestTodo_ASSURANCE_001_Mutation`, plus `TestAssessmentValidateRejectsMissingMetadataAndFindingIntegrity`, `TestRegisterGateClaimAndAddErrorPaths` and `TestAssessmentValidateAllowsNonCriticalFindingStatuses` in `internal/operations/assurance` (`register.go`); `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/operations/assurance/` PASS at 96.6% coverage on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. Verified against the contract rather than taken on the strength of a green run: `Assessment.Validate` requires `AssessorIndependent`, refuses an assessment whose `Expires` is zero or not after its `Date`, and refuses evidence once `now` reaches `Expires`, so expiry is enforced rather than advisory; every finding must carry id, owner, deadline and severity, duplicates are refused, and a CRITICAL or HIGH finding must additionally be `RETESTED` with a non-nil retest that is `Independent`, results in a pass, and names an assessor and date -- so an open critical finding cannot validate and therefore cannot permit the gate. `Register.Gate` returns `Decision{Reasons: ["no assurance evidence"]}` for an empty register, whose `Allowed` is the zero value false, so absence fails closed, and it iterates assessment ids in sorted order for a deterministic decision. `Claim` carries exact scope and excluded surfaces and its statement ends "This statement is not a certification", which is the GREEN clause about not implying unattained certification. No behaviour was changed: this todo was implemented but unticked, which reads as work nobody started.
