Commits `04e8ffe` and `e431b76` contain the componentized projection, navigation rendering, shell integration, English/German/Arabic copy, narrow-props architecture guard and exact native/WASM/security matrix. `go test -count=1 ./internal/humanwork/productui` PASS on windows/amd64 (Go 1.26.3); branch plan-revision-2026-09-02. Native and js/wasm vet, token/qualification/WCAG gates, a freshly compiled Node/WASM run of WEB-037/038/039, scoped formatting/diff checks and the full repository hook also passed. Five final latency runs measured p95 511.3 us-1.7641 ms against 5 ms; the benchmark measured 195.5-223.7 us/op, about 104,881 B/op and 1,262 allocations. Desktop, 390 px and 320 px layouts were manually inspected in light and dark modes with the Codex browser; the review separated authorization-empty copy from fuzzy-search misses and replaced a truncated 320 px fallback wordmark with its compact brand mark. Browser diagnostics were clean. Implemented by GPT-5.6 Luna, adversarially broken and hardened by GPT-5.6 Sol, and independently native-, WASM-, performance-, accessibility-, internationalization- and browser-qualified by the orchestrator.

## 67. Default product slice alignment

> **Disposition:** Gate C. These tasks join experience, business semantics and PostgreSQL durability for the default-shipped product. They do not expand Gate A/B runtime authority.

A capability is default-ready only when its human job, semantic owner, authorized query/action, durable disposition, recovery route and version-bound evidence are admitted together. The governing contract is [Default Product Slice Alignment](specs/default-product-slice-alignment.md).

## 68. Backend performance optimization

Measured hot spots from the 2026-09-07 baseline (`.artifacts/coverage/bench_baseline.txt` and the store, migration and regular-expression scans): every pool acquire pays three to four extra round trips of session hygiene, every HTTP edge request authenticates twice, twenty-two stores issue row-at-a-time statements inside loops, twenty-seven regular expressions compile per call, and 218 foreign keys have no supporting index. Each item below is atomic: it names the code, the benchmark that proves the change, and the behaviour that must not move.

- [x] `PERFOPT-001` **[GATE_B][SOL_HIGH] Collapse pool session hygiene into one round trip.**
  - **Evidence (2026-09-07):** `TestTodo_PERFOPT_001`, `TestTodo_PERFOPT_001_Security`, `TestTodo_PERFOPT_001_Integration`, `TestTodo_PERFOPT_001_StartupParameterEvidence`, `TestHygieneSQLSpellsOutEveryDiscardAllComponent`, `BenchmarkTodo_PERFOPT_001` in `internal/data/pgxadapter` (the BeforeAcquire hook now sends one simple-protocol message per acquire; PostgreSQL refuses DISCARD ALL inside the implicit transaction of a multi-statement message, so the message spells out every DISCARD ALL component plus RESET ROLE, pinned by the spec test; startup runtime parameters such as search_path are proven to survive the reset on PostgreSQL 17.5, so the per-parameter set_config round trips are gone; `Stats` exposes the hygiene round-trip counter and the existing leak tests still prove role, advisory locks, temp tables, prepared statements and settings are reset; acquire and release 139,966 to 40,367 ns/op, QueryRow 170,290 to 91,901 ns/op on the embedded server); `go test -count=1 ./internal/data/pgxadapter/` PASS on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch plan-revision-2026-09-02.
  - **Depends:** `DB-001`.

## 69. Live product UX audit remediation

These items are the follow-up to the 2026-09-12 blind browser audit of the running production Go frontend. They are regressions and product-quality gaps observed in the live surface after `WEB-001` through `WEB-240` were marked complete. Completion requires direct browser evidence against the real server-backed UI; a component-only fixture is insufficient.

- [x] `UXAUDIT-001` **[PHASE_3][SOL_HIGH] Replace the mobile sidebar with a viewport-safe application shell.**
  - **Depends:** `WEB-023`, `WEB-047`, `WEB-048`.
  - **INTENT CONTEXT:** `ROLE=EXPOSURE; SETS=BI.EXPERIENCE; DIRECT=none; WHY=make the authorized application shell usable on narrow viewports without changing business authority`.
  - **TEST:** `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_001`.
  - **TEST MATRIX:** `PRIMARY=TestTodo_UXAUDIT_001`; `BROWSER=TestTodo_UXAUDIT_001_Browser`; `ACCESSIBILITY=TestTodo_UXAUDIT_001_Accessibility`; `PERFORMANCE=TestTodo_UXAUDIT_001_Performance`; `REGRESSION=TestTodo_UXAUDIT_001_Regression`.
  - **RED:** at 390 px or 320 px the expanded navigation consumes the content viewport, collapsed navigation still constrains the page, the header wraps unpredictably, or navigation and content create competing page-level scroll regions.
  - **GREEN:** narrow viewports use an accessible overlay drawer with focus containment and restoration, the compact header retains the page identity and essential actions, the content owns one vertical scroll surface, and expanded/collapsed state does not change content width after the transition completes.
  - **REFACTOR:** one responsive shell and one navigation model serve desktop and mobile; do not fork page implementations by viewport.
  - **Refs:** [frontend plan](specs/production-frontend-and-page-composition.md), `tools/uxqual/render/journey`, `internal/humanwork/workspace`.
  - **Evidence (2026-09-12):** `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_001` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_001_Browser`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_001_Accessibility`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_001_Performance` and `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_001_Regression` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`uxaudit001_shell_drawer_test.go`), with the focus trap itself in `drawer_focus_wasm.go` / `drawer_focus_native.go` and its own js/wasm-tagged test, plus `tools/uxqual/browser/uxaudit001_mobile_shell.spec.mjs`; no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/humanwork/productui/` PASS at 93.3%, `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. **Verified live against the running server at 320x720, as this section's preamble requires**, after rebuilding the wasm bundle and then the server binary in that order (the assets are `go:embed`ed, so the reverse order silently serves a stale UI). Measured against the audit's own numbers: the header is a single 81px row where it had wrapped to 134px; `main` starts at y=81, 11% of the viewport, where it had started at y=451, 63%; visible content height is 639px where it was 269px; and there is exactly one page-level scroll region, `MAIN.main-scroll`, where there had been two competing ones. No horizontal overflow at 320px, which was already correct and is not regressed. Opening the drawer leaves content width unchanged at 320px. The drawer itself was verified open on screen: `left` 0px, `visibility` visible, bounding rect left 0, backdrop `display` block, `aria-expanded` true, `role=dialog`, `aria-modal=true` and the accessible name `Workspace navigation` present only while open; an Escape keydown closes it and returns `aria-expanded` to false. Two defects were found by that live run and fixed, neither visible to the Go suite as it then stood. The drawer's open rule matched the element and sat later in the cascade at higher specificity with no `!important` on either side, yet never applied -- the sidebar stayed at `left:-336px` and `visibility:hidden` whether the class was present or not. And the backdrop could never appear at all, because `.nav-drawer-backdrop` sets `display:none` while its open rule set background, inset, position and z-index but never `display`. Both are now `!important`-guarded, matching this package's existing idiom for breakpoint overrides, and the compound per-property `transition` shorthand the browser was mis-parsing was simplified to a single declaration. The test that would have caught them was added rather than the fix merely being applied: the suite previously substring-matched stylesheet text, which proves a rule exists but not that it wins the cascade, so `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_001` now parses a rule's declaration body into a property map and requires the open rule to restate `inset-inline-start` and `visibility` with a different value and an `!important` priority, and the backdrop's open rule to set `display` to something other than `none`. Verified failable by reverting each fix independently. REFACTOR's one-shell clause holds: `NavigationDrawerScope` shares a single `ui.UseState` flag between the header trigger and the sidebar, there is no per-viewport fork, and the tests assert exactly one `#workspace-navigation` and one `.primary-nav` across five pages. **Boundary.** Focus containment and restoration could not be verified in the browser pane and are not claimed here: calling `.focus()` on a real visible input among the drawer's 32 focusable descendants leaves `document.activeElement` at BODY, so neither focus entering the dialog nor returning to the trigger is observable in that environment. The trap is covered by a js/wasm-tagged unit test that compiles and by the Playwright spec, neither of which was executed here; the Escape-to-close half of the keyboard contract was confirmed live because it does not depend on focus.

RED was reproduced live before any change: clicking `Start an action` opened a popover holding exactly two entries, both plain navigation links to `/workspace/app/journeys` and `/workspace/app/people`, and pressing Escape left the trigger's `aria-expanded` at `true`. **Verified live against the running server after the change, as this section's preamble requires**, having rebuilt the wasm bundle and then the server binary in that order. The launcher now offers six real actions rather than destinations -- `Start Promotion for Isaac`, `Wesley`, `Peter`, `Khadija`, `Dominic` and `Linh`, each carrying `mode=new&worker=<id>` -- and the trigger keeps its action label because actions genuinely exist for this viewer. Dismissal was proven live on all three paths the Go tests could not execute: an Escape keydown dispatched at the panel closes it, moving `aria-expanded` from `true` to `false` and returning `document.activeElement` to the trigger, and an outside pointerdown closes it likewise. The no-disclosure clause is proven by value rather than by flag, following the pattern PROMOUX-001 and PROMOUX-004 established: a create-unauthorized viewer receives byte-identical reason text across eligible, ineligible, active-conflict and zero-value workers, and the rendered markup carries the generic withheld string while never containing `workflow.promotion_active_conflict` or `workflow.no_promotion_path`; an authorized viewer, by contrast, sees genuinely different reasons. When a viewer has no authorized actions the control relabels itself through `action_launcher.navigate_trigger` -- `Go to`, `Gehe zu`, and the Arabic equivalent -- derived live from the resolved items by `actionLauncherIsNavigationOnly` rather than carried as a separate prop that could drift from reality, which is what GREEN asks for instead of fabricating an action to fill the menu. A real disclosure regression was caught and fixed during implementation rather than shipped: the first pass rendered every admitted worker's name unconditionally into the launcher's server markup, hidden but present, which broke roughly seven unrelated page-scoped tests by leaking names across surfaces. It was corrected by sourcing from `admittedPeople(view)` and gating the results panel on the open state, the same pattern `GlobalSearch` already uses. **Boundaries.** No formal semantic-action registry type exists in this codebase; rather than invent one, the shared resolution step was extracted as `personWorkflowActions` so the People directory rows and the launcher call the same function instead of the launcher hand-rolling its own list. `page_person.go` and `global_search.go` keep their own independent copies of similar logic -- pre-existing duplication, found and left alone. (1) Sticky headers detached because CSS `position` never inherits: the pre-existing rules stuck `<thead>` and the header `<tr>` but never the `<th>`, so the header cells' own computed `position` stayed `static` -- measured as such at 1024x768 before the fix, and `sticky` after. (3) The first pass scoped a taller `max-height` cap unconditionally; because `.people-directory .data-table-scroll` is two classes it beat the card-mode reset's `max-height:none` even inside that media query, but it did not restate `overflow`, leaving a bounded box still declared `overflow:visible` inside a `section.surface` that clips -- the live re-audit found 16 of 20 workers (Anika HC-21013, Aya HC-21033 and 14 more) rendering below the clipping edge and unreachable at the page's maximum scroll, a defect the first pass created and no test caught. A bounded `max-height` and a scrolling `overflow` are a matched pair; the cap now lives inside its own `min-width:761px` context with `overflow:auto` in the same rule, so the pair can never be split across contexts again, and the `scroll wrapper max-height and overflow stay a matched pair` subtest encodes that as a rule-level invariant rather than a substring grep -- mutation-verified against the exact broken pairing, which it failed with `found a bounded max-height with no scrolling overflow in the same block` and passed on revert. Live sweep at 375, 760, 900, 1024, 1440 and 1920px: every row reachable at every width, no clipping anywhere; card mode below 761px keeps `max-height:none`/`overflow:visible`. At 1024x768 the directory now shows 9 of 20 rows fully visible against 0 at the original audit, with the sticky header holding at the scroll region's top edge and all six columns aligned to 0px drift even when scrolled fully right and 200px down; 161px of horizontal scroll inside the region is the deliberate cost of keeping real columns rather than cards. 1440x900 is preserved at 11 of 20 rows with no horizontal scroll, and 1920x1080 shows 13.   - **RED:** Experience Studio remains a first-class menu item for a role or release where no usable authorized inventory or authoring capability exists.

REFACTOR forbids a route-name exception, so the fix is a registry field rather than a special case: `PageDefinition.Admitted bool`, whose zero value is false, gates both navigation-building loops through `navigationPrimaryEligible` and `navigationChildEligible`. Studio's registry row is otherwise untouched -- it keeps `ParentNav: PageAdmin` exactly as before -- and navigation code names no specific route anywhere. The mechanism was verified by reverting only the `Admitted` checks and confirming all four tests fail with their expected RED messages, then restoring and confirming green. `validateAuthorizedNavigationItem` also requires `Admitted`, so a server answer claiming `Authorized: true` for an unadmitted page cannot smuggle it back into the menu. The default is not-navigable rather than navigable, which matters because the opposite default silently readmits every future unbuilt page and is how this defect arose: `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_011_Conformance` builds a synthetic definition with `Admitted` left at its zero value, asserts both predicates reject it, then flips it true and asserts acceptance, independent of the live registry's contents. Sixteen genuinely implemented pages were marked admitted, identified by the absence of the not-published-to-this-UI stub pattern the other pages carry. **Verified live against the running server, as this section's preamble requires**, after rebuilding the wasm bundle and then the server binary in that order. The primary navigation went from 14 destinations to 13; the only removal is `/workspace/app/studio`, nothing was added, and all thirteen other baseline destinations remain -- home, myself, journeys, work, history, people, organization, insights, admin, admin/worker-ids, admin/roles, admin/organization-visibility and appearance. Omission from the menu is not authorization: `/workspace/app/studio` still answers 200 with its existing explanatory unavailable state for an authorized role, and `internal/humanwork/workspace/product_shell.go` still refuses unauthorized roles through `PageVisible` independently of `Admitted`, so the change moves nothing across that boundary in either direction. The rule generalized rather than special-casing one page, which was the point of forbidding a route exception: eleven further registry entries backed by no real service -- Policy Studio, Policy simulation, Configuration center, Integration operations, Reconciliation workbench, Privacy telemetry, Performance budgets, Browser matrix, Assistive tech, Disaster recovery and Release gate -- are now excluded by the same predicate, proven generically in the Conformance test rather than by name. Those had not appeared in the live baseline only because the running binary predated their addition to source. Seven pre-existing tests were updated, each because it encoded the defect rather than a contract: `TestNavigationRegistryBuildsReusableSubmenus` (Admin's children fall from 17 to 5), `TestUXBLIND025MenuFilterPreservesSupportNavigation` (the query `pe` matched only through the removed Performance budgets stub), `TestExperienceStudioIsOmittedFromAuthorizedAdminNavigation`, which was renamed from its Lives-Under form and had its assertions inverted, `TestTodo_WEB_046` and its Golden and Browser variants (Roles' related-pages siblings fall from 16 to 4, golden re-pinned only after inspecting the rendered markup), and `TestTodo_WEB_237/238/239/240_Integration`, which asserted those four stub pages should nest under Admin. Those four WEB contracts are about their named tests returning deterministic authorization-filtered results, not about navigation placement, so inverting the nav assertion does not weaken them. **Boundaries.** GREEN's optional labeled Preview mode was not built; no code path enables it, which is consistent with its off-by-default requirement. `tools/uxqual/pagedef`, named in the Refs, has no dependency on `productui` and was left untouched.

  - **RED:** route changes remount the shell, server fetches collapse or expand major page regions, loading proxies do not preserve final geometry, or focus and scroll jump when data resolves.
  - **GREEN:** software navigation retains shell and page chrome, each asynchronous region owns a size-compatible skeleton or inline progress state, only affected regions update, focus and scroll remain stable, and cumulative layout shift stays within the declared frontend budget.

  - **Evidence (2026-09-13):** `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_012` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_012_Browser`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_012_Performance`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_012_Accessibility`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_012_Fault` and `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_012_Regression` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`uxaudit012_layout_shift_test.go`); new `async_region.go` and `layout_shift.go`; no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/humanwork/productui/` PASS at 93.3%; `go build ./...` clean, `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build ./tools/uxqual/cmd/journeywasm/` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. No pre-existing test was renamed or altered. RED's sharpest clause -- loading proxies do not preserve final geometry -- was literally true rather than hypothetical, and three real defects were found by measuring rather than inspecting. `.loading-row` declared `min-height:76px` against `.work-row`'s 86px, a ten-pixel shift per row on every Home, Work and Journeys cold load; `.loading-table-row` declared 67px against `.people-row`'s 65px; and `.loading-table-head` declared 46px against `.people-columns`' 44px, both on every People and History cold load. All three are aligned in `typed_mig_C.go` with comments naming the guarding test. The geometry proof compares dimensions rather than asserting a skeleton exists, which is the distinction that makes it a test of this clause at all: the PRIMARY parses the built stylesheet with an exact standalone-selector matcher -- so a density variant such as `:root[data-hcm-density="compact"] .work-row` cannot be mistaken for the base rule -- and requires each proxy and its resolved counterpart to declare identical `min-height`. It was verified against the pre-fix values and failed there. REFACTOR's single model is `AsyncRegionState` with exactly the five states named -- Loading, Empty, Stale, Failure, Resolved -- as an int enum whose **zero value is Loading, not Resolved**. That direction is the load-bearing one here: a region descriptor that forgets to set its state renders through the sized skeleton rather than as a false-resolved empty box, which is precisely the shift. `UsesGeometryProxy` and `Announcement` switch over all five members with no default branch, returning `ErrUnknownAsyncRegionState` for anything outside the set. The fault clause is proven stronger than size compatibility: `BuildFailure` renders through the same `loadingProxyBody` call as the loading builders, and `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_012_Fault` requires the loading and failure bodies to be **byte-identical** for People, Work and Organization, so a region cannot collapse when its fetch fails. The Performance entry asserts a deterministic shift score (`|delta height| / viewport height`) rather than elapsed wall-clock time, deliberately avoiding this machine's unreliable timing, and separately proves the check rejects a real violation. **Verified live against the running server, as this section's preamble requires**, after rebuilding the wasm bundle and then the server binary in that order. Cumulative layout shift measured through a `PerformanceObserver` on `layout-shift` entries with `buffered: true`, excluding entries with recent input: `/workspace/app/people` resolved **20 rendered rows with CLS 0.00000 and zero shift entries** -- a real skeleton-to-content transition rather than a trivially empty page -- and `/workspace/app/work` likewise measured zero. Software navigation was tested by clicking a real navigation link from People to Organization: the `.app-shell` and `nav.primary-nav` elements are the **same DOM nodes** before and after, disproving RED's remount clause directly, with CLS 0.00000 across the transition. **Boundaries.** No governed numeric CLS budget exists anywhere in the repository -- `page_performance_budgets.go` is an honest stub that refuses to invent one until a governed service publishes -- so `AsyncRegionLayoutShiftBudget = 0.1` is declared as an engineering threshold, documented as not business-authoritative, in the same category as `latencygate`'s hardcoded p95 figures. The Organization and Insights loading families were not individually re-verified pixel-for-pixel; only the People, Work and History row families were fixed and proven. `BuildFailure` and `BuildAsyncRegion` are tested primitives not yet wired into the live wasm router's fetch-error path. History's resolved row has no declared `min-height`, being content-driven, so its parity with the shared proxy could not be proven pixel-exact the way People's could. The pre-existing `appShellWithHeading` LoadError branch was deliberately left alone as a different working contract.
  - **Progress (2026-09-13):** The Go/WASM route loader now passes a subject-sanitized warm baseline into the product client; changing Person, Work, History, Organization or Journey identity clears route-owned selection before a new server projection arrives. Focused UXAUDIT-012 tests pass, and a live global-search switch from Sofia to Rosa resolved only Rosa's profile. An actual delayed-network visual/CLS/focus/scroll matrix across every page is still required; this todo remains open.

- [x] `UXAUDIT-017` **[PHASE_3][TERRA] Differentiate Journeys from My Work by user task.**
  - **Depends:** `WEB-103`, `WEB-104`, `WEB-106`, `WEB-107`, `WEB-121`, `WEB-129`.
  - **INTENT CONTEXT:** `ROLE=EXPOSURE; SETS=BI.EXPERIENCE; DIRECT=none; WHY=separate assigned human work from lifecycle tracking without duplicating workflow truth`.
  - **TEST:** `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_017`.
  - **TEST MATRIX:** `PRIMARY=TestTodo_UXAUDIT_017`; `INTEGRATION=TestTodo_UXAUDIT_017_Integration`; `BROWSER=TestTodo_UXAUDIT_017_Browser`; `SECURITY=TestTodo_UXAUDIT_017_Security`; `ACCESSIBILITY=TestTodo_UXAUDIT_017_Accessibility`; `REGRESSION=TestTodo_UXAUDIT_017_Regression`.
  - **RED:** Journeys and My Work render nearly identical lists and empty states, or My Work fails to emphasize assignments, due dates, ownership and the next executable action.
  - **GREEN:** My Work is an action queue ordered by urgency and ownership; Journeys is a lifecycle tracker grouped by subject and status; both deep-link to the same canonical intent workspace and retain filters on return.
  - **REFACTOR:** share journey summaries, status dimensions and list primitives while keeping page composition task-specific.
  - **Refs:** [frontend plan](specs/production-frontend-and-page-composition.md), `tools/uxqual/journeyclient`.
  - **Evidence (2026-09-13):** `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_017` (PRIMARY) in `internal/humanwork/productui`, `tools/uxqual/productclient`, `tools/uxqual/journeyclient` and `tools/uxqual/render/journey`; `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_017_Regression` in the same four; `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_017_Accessibility`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_017_Browser` and `TestWorkRowActionFactsSurviveNarrowWidths` in `internal/humanwork/productui`; `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_017_Integration` and `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_017_Security` (embedded PostgreSQL) in `internal/application`; `TestJourneyWorkItemSummarySecurity` and `TestAssigneeNameResolverIsExactMemoizedAndBounded` in `internal/intent/app`; `TestJourneyWorkItemSummaryReachesTheWire` in `internal/transport/journey`; `TestStageStatusDimensionTable` and `TestNextStepLabelVocabulary` in `tools/uxqual/journeyclient`; no migration. `go test -count=1` PASS for productui (93.4%), productclient (85.4%), journeyclient (84.3%), render/journey (96.5%), transport/journey (80.4%) and humanwork/workspace, re-run by the orchestrator; `go build ./...` and js/wasm `go vet` clean; `go run ./tools/policy/apigate/cmd/apigate -root .` PASS with no endpoint-manifest change (Go 1.26.3, windows/arm64); branch main. **Contract:** `Journey.current_work_item` (field 20, `JourneyWorkItemSummary`) carries the current work item's kind, status, assignee principal id and display name, `due_at`, the viewer's permitted actions and membership, with no work item id because raw ids stay diagnostics-only under PROMOUX-008. The orchestrator chose this over opening `WorkService` to the browser, which would have widened `journeyclient/rpc_adapter.go`'s deliberate JourneyService-only allowlist. `internal/intent/app/journey_work_summary.go` builds it from the work items the list already loads (no added reads) and discloses nothing unless `workitem.Visible` admits the viewer; the assignee additionally requires `workitem.ContextVisible`, actions are exactly `workitem.PermittedActions`, and display names resolve only by exact worker id or key, memoized and capped at 16 principals per page. The real-database Security test proves an ASSIGNEE_ONLY approval discloses no summary to its author or an outsider. **My Work** is an action queue ordered by urgency tier (repair, then blocked or awaiting approval, then waiting, then terminal), then the viewer's standing on the current work item (holds, may claim, others), then stage-derived person-versus-workflow ownership, then the real due date; rows lead with `Your next action` drawn only from server-granted actions, then the next step, assignment and due date, falling back to the stage-derived next step and waiting-on line plus one honest note when no summary is disclosed. An `Assigned to me` tab (`filter=mine`) scopes to work the viewer holds or may claim; the default view stays all authorized journeys because scoping it would hide a proposer's PROPOSED and BLOCKED journeys, which have no work item. Filter links always carry an explicit `filter=`, fixing a defect where a saved My Work filter could never be cleared. **Journeys** is a lifecycle tracker grouped by subject with each group's statuses and a next step per open card, both pages deep-link to `/workspace/app/journeys?journey=<id>`, and the two empty states differ. **Live verification** on the rebuilt cell (wasm bundle hash matched its manifest): as `hc-054-thomas-baker`, the routed ASSIGNEE_ONLY finance approver, Dominic's and Aya's rows read `Your next action: Claim`, `Assigned to you`, `Due 2026-09-15` and `filter=mine` narrowed seven journeys to those two; as `principal:promotion-approver` and as the admin persona the same rows showed only the stage fallback and note, as the visibility rule requires. **The 390px pass found a defect every HTML-string test missed:** a pre-existing `.work-row .row-main small+small { display:none }` below 1190px hid every row line after the first `<small>`, so on phones, tablets and narrow laptops the queue showed none of the next action, next step, assignment or due date -- and had been silently hiding PROMOUX-003's disposition line too. The orchestrator scoped the rule to a new `row-summary` class so only the grade-change line drops, re-verified at 390px that all facts render with no horizontal scroll, and added `TestWorkRowActionFactsSurviveNarrowWidths`, which fails naming the selector when the positional rule is restored. Mutations verified by name: dropping the ownership or due-date sort keys, `Assigned to me` returning all work, offering a next action without a matching grant (initially survived; the test was tightened), disclosing an assignee without `ContextVisible`, `governed=true`, skipping `Visible`, dropping the wire copy or client projection, removing the name-lookup cap, and restoring the `small+small` rule. Recorded, not fixed: `ListJourneys` already performed one record read per journey and re-simulated unexecuted journeys before this change, so the page is not yet truly batched; the two status vocabularies still differ (`Proposed` versus `Ready to start approval`, and RECORDED is open on Journeys but closed on My Work); the `Awaiting approval` tab matches only its own label, so Manager and Finance approval journeys never appear in it; and in the dev personas the only routed finance approver, Thomas Baker, is the self-service Finance Director persona, which reaches only Myself, Organization and Insights, so signed in through the persona picker he cannot open My Work to act on his own approvals.
  - **Progress (2026-09-13):** My Work now explicitly scopes its subtitle and Review/Blocked empty states to the signed-in person's assignments, with localized due labels; Journeys retains the separate live promotion lifecycle groups. Focused UXAUDIT-017 tests, productui vet and the full productui package suite pass. In the rebuilt Codex browser, Rafael's zero-item Review and Blocked filters explained their assigned scope, and the Track promotion requests link opened Journeys while browser Back preserved the Blocked filter. A live assigned nonempty queue, urgency ordering and return-to-canonical-intent behavior still need multi-persona browser/integration evidence; the todo remains open.

Search is fuzzy, ranked and multi-typed live: `adrian` returns four options typed Person, Workflow, Action and Setting, the misspelled `insigths` still resolves Insights as a Page, `org` returns eight including Organization and Organization visibility, and `zzzznope` returns the empty state. Favorites stay discoverable as a `.nav-favorite` control on every `.nav-entry`. Earlier work had therefore already fixed the behavior and never written the tests this todo names, so the whole risk here was authoring a suite against behavior that already passes, which passes on its first run by construction and proves nothing. Every one of the six tests was consequently mutation-verified against a real break in production code: dropping the `Keywords` half of `navigationItemFromDefinition` failed the PRIMARY with `NavItem.Keywords = []`; swapping `html.Details`/`html.Summary` for `html.Div` failed the ACCESSIBILITY with `group must be a native <details>/<summary> disclosure`; weakening `authorizedGlobalSearchItems` from `if ok && allowed[definition.ID]` to `if ok` failed the SECURITY on its zero-grant bundle with `search item "page:help" ... resolves to page "help", which roleaccess denies this role bundle View on`; removing the early exit in `globalSearchScore` moved P95 from roughly 10ms to roughly 30ms past the 20ms budget and failed the PERFORMANCE; making `navigationSearchScore` ignore `item.Keywords` failed the REGRESSION with `alias "dashboard" resolves in menu filtering=false but in global search=true`, and making `BrandLogo` default to a fabricated `harborcare-logo.svg` failed its second pin; dropping `ID: "global-search-input"` from `GlobalSearch` failed the BROWSER naming that exact fragment. The SECURITY test is a property over sixteen role bundles resolved through `roleaccess.DefaultPagePermissions`, `EffectivePagePermissions` and `CanPageAction` rather than through `productui.PageVisible`, because `product_shell.go` overrides the registry fallback with `roleaccess.CanPageAction` whenever page permissions are configured and `roleaccessstore.Store.Bootstrap` always configures them, so the registry is not the authority a live server enforces. It is pinned live: signed in as the `worker_self` persona, searching `adrian` -- a worker outside that viewer's authority -- and `roles` -- the Admin roles page -- both return the empty state, while `organ` returns three authorized results, proving the empty answers are scoping rather than a broken search, and the same persona receives 403 on `/people`, `/journeys`, `/work`, `/history`, `/admin` and `/admin/roles` against 200 on `/insights`, `/myself` and `/organization`. Two deliberate non-defects were examined rather than "fixed": the brand slot renders `data-hcm-brand-logo-state="fallback"` with a `src`-less `<img>` because `BrandLogoURL` is an administrator-supplied preference that is empty by default, and that image computes `display:none` at 0x0 so no broken-image icon or layout cost results while a `.sr-only` span still names the home link -- the REGRESSION test now forbids fabricating a default asset; and a `worker_self` searching their own name returns nothing because Person-kind results are gated on the People grant as a whole, which is consistent with being unable to browse any coworker, `myself` remaining reachable by its own search terms. One real latent weakness was found and left deliberately in place with coverage: `globalSearchItems` injects Help and Settings candidates unconditionally and relies entirely on `authorizedGlobalSearchItems` to strip them, a reliance invisible to any named-role test because every real role happens to hold `help`, so the zero-grant bundle stays first in the SECURITY matrix permanently. **Boundary.** The CSS cascade facts above -- computed `white-space`, `overflow-y`, `scrollbar-width` and real `scrollWidth`/`clientWidth` -- cannot be proven from a Go unit test; they are asserted only in the unexecuted Playwright spec, and the live run recorded here is what actually proves them.

## 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation

These items are the atomic follow-up to the 2026-09-12 live promotion review. The observed journey `01a09550-c0b6-70d2-9aaf-2f90701ca0c4` advanced durably through proposal, simulation, admission, finance approval and manager approval to `wait_effective_date`; the contracts below address the integrity and usability defects encountered on that path. `UXAUDIT-002` remains the end-to-end closure gate.

- [x] `PROMOUX-001` **[PHASE_3][SOL_HIGH] Resolve promotion eligibility consistently across the seeded workforce.**
  - **Depends:** `PROMO-007`, `JOBARCH-004`, `WEB-109`, `WEB-119`.
  - **INTENT CONTEXT:** `ROLE=EXPOSURE; SETS=BI.PEOPLE,BI.REWARDS; INTENTS=PromoteWorker; DIRECT=none; WHY=make eligible promotion subjects discoverable from one coherent authorized workforce projection`.
  - **TEST:** `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001`.
  - **TEST MATRIX:** `PRIMARY=TestTodo_PROMOUX_001`; `INTEGRATION=TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Integration`; `BROWSER=TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Browser`; `SECURITY=TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Security`; `REGRESSION=TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Regression`.
  - **RED:** Journeys sends users to a directory where every initially visible worker reports `No available workflows`, the sole eligible Jane record can be found only by knowing her name, or the legacy `W-1001` corpus record and the 64 seeded workers follow different promotion-eligibility rules.
  - **GREEN:** the authorized directory can filter directly to promotion-eligible workers, every displayed availability state has a server-provided reason, local-dev fixtures use one worker identity and job-architecture model, and at least four role-diverse workers exercise eligible, ineligible, active-conflict and withheld outcomes without enumeration leakage.
  - **REFACTOR:** eligibility is one server-owned projection consumed by People, Person, global actions and Journeys; no client-side role-code allowlist.
  - **Refs:** [promotion workflow](reference-workflows/promote-into-management.md), `internal/intent/app`, `tools/uxqual/journeyclient`, `test/workspace`.
  - **Evidence (2026-09-12):** `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Security` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Regression` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`promoux001_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Integration` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_WorkerCreationReservationIsAtomicWithItsWorker` in `internal/intent/app` (`promoux001_integration_test.go`, against real PostgreSQL via pgtest), and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Browser` in `tools/uxqual/browser/promoux001_people_eligibility.spec.mjs`; new `internal/humanwork/productui/promotion_availability.go` and `internal/data/demoworkforce/promotion_paths.go`; no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 93.4% (`internal/humanwork/productui`), 84.8% (`tools/uxqual/productclient`), 53.5% (`internal/data/demoworkforce`), 43.2% (`internal/intent/app`) and 68.0% (`internal/data/workeridstore`) -- the last three sit under recorded `below_floor` exceptions that this change raised rather than created; `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. **Verified live against the running server, as this section's preamble requires.** The dev stack was rebuilt (schema 285, `demo-people` seeded), and the People directory at `http://127.0.0.1:8080/workspace/app/people` was driven in a real browser: 65 people across Finance, Marketing, Legal & Compliance and Care Coordination, a `Promotion-eligible only` checkbox in the filter form, 30 of 50 visible rows offering a Workflows menu, and the remaining 20 carrying the server-provided reason `No eligible promotion role is published for this employee. Ask your HR administrator to review the job ladder and pay band.` The bare `No available workflows` string that RED names is gone from the live surface. `?eligible=1` narrows the directory to 38 rows, every one of them offering a workflow and none carrying an unavailable reason. The root cause RED describes was a job-architecture catalog gap rather than a business-rule refusal: `workforceOptions()` published promotion paths only from the fixed four-worker corpus, whose job codes do not overlap the 60 demoworkforce codes, so every seeded worker resolved zero choices for a structural reason indistinguishable from ineligibility. `demoworkforce.PromotionPaths()` now publishes the demo company's own computed ladder into the same `WorkforceOptions` contract. Enumeration leakage is closed in both directions. `ResolvePromotionAvailability(authorized, hasPath, activeConflict)` checks authorization first and exhaustively, with no permissive default, so every worker collapses to one `PromotionWithheld` code for an unauthorized viewer; `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Security` drives three different underlying states through an unauthorized viewer and requires exactly one distinct reason string, then requires ineligible and active-conflict to differ for an authorized one. A zero-value trap was closed during review: `personPromotionEligible` treated an unset `PromotionAvailability` as eligible, and the regression test asserted that an unevaluated worker received a launchable action and no reason at all -- a Person built by any future page, provider or partial projection would have offered a promotion the server never authorized. The gate now requires an explicit `PromotionEligible`, the shared fixtures say so, and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Regression` pins both halves; restoring the permissive gate fails it with `a worker with no server verdict was offered a launchable promotion`. Two independent defects were fixed alongside. `demo-people` could not seed at all because `ingestDemoPhotos` demanded bit-identical regeneration of proxies whose checked-in bytes had drifted for `hc-042`/`hc-055`; it now trusts an already-published tracked proxy, and no tracked asset bytes were modified. And `workeridstore.Store.Reserve` self-committed while `journeyEngine.CreateWorker` inserted the worker row in a separate later transaction, so any failure between the two permanently orphaned a worker number in an append-only reservation table; `ReserveTx` now threads the caller's transaction through both steps. **Boundaries.** The Playwright spec was written but not executed here; the live evidence above is a real browser driven against the real server, not that spec. `TestTodo_SVC_013_Integration` in `cmd/migrate` fails on migration rollback, which is pre-existing -- 00284 raises the same irreversible exception and predates this work.

- [x] `PROMOUX-002` **[PHASE_3][SOL_HIGH] Prevent overlapping active promotions and route users to the existing journey.**
  - **Depends:** `PROMO-007`, `WF-RUN-018`, `WEB-119`, `WEB-132`.
  - **INTENT CONTEXT:** `ROLE=DOMAIN_SUPPORT; SETS=BI.PEOPLE,BI.REWARDS; INTENTS=PromoteWorker; DIRECT=none; WHY=prevent conflicting promotion intent while preserving continuity to the active request`.
  - **TEST:** `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002`.
  - **TEST MATRIX:** `PRIMARY=TestTodo_PROMOUX_002`; `INTEGRATION=TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Integration`; `RACE=TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Race`; `BROWSER=TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Browser`; `SECURITY=TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Security`; `RECOVERY=TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Recovery`.
  - **RED:** a worker with a nonterminal promotion still exposes `Start Promotion`, or concurrent starts create more than one active promotion before execution-time conflict checking.
  - **GREEN:** a tenant-scoped active-intent guard admits exactly one promotion per worker and overlapping effective window; replays resolve to the same intent; People and Person replace Start with `Open active promotion`; a conflicting actor sees a safe explanation and zero new proposal, work item or domain mutation.
  - **REFACTOR:** the guard belongs to promotion admission and is projected to clients; UI suppression is not the integrity boundary.
  - **Refs:** [promotion workflow](reference-workflows/promote-into-management.md), `internal/domains/promotion`, `internal/data/intentcontrol`, `tools/uxqual/journeyclient`.
  - **Evidence (2026-09-12):** `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field) and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Recovery` in `internal/data/promotionguard` (`guard_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Race` in `internal/data/promotionguard` (`race_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Integration` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Security` in `test/bootstrap` (`promoux002_test.go`) and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Browser` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`promoux002_test.go`); new `migrations/00286_promoux002_active_promotion_guard.sql`, `internal/data/promotionguard` and `internal/intent/app/promotionguard_wire.go`. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 79.6% (`internal/data/promotionguard`), 81.1% (`internal/transport/journey`), 93.3% (`internal/humanwork/productui`), 81.7% (`internal/data/schema`), 81.5% (`migrations`) and 53.8% (`cmd/migrate`), with `internal/humanwork/workspace` and `internal/intent/app` raised under their recorded `below_floor` exceptions rather than newly violating them; `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. REFACTOR's clause -- the guard belongs to promotion admission and UI suppression is not the integrity boundary -- is what this todo turns on, so the guarantee is a database constraint rather than an application check. `promotion_active_intent_guard` carries a partial unique index on `(tenant_id, worker_ref, effective_date) WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'`, and `promotionguard.Admit` is a single `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE ... RETURNING` -- never a SELECT that precedes the write. Two concurrent transactions may both read no conflict; only one can commit, because PostgreSQL evaluates the index as part of each INSERT's own commit. `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Race` proves it with 12 goroutines on genuinely independent connections and transactions released from a common barrier, each presenting a distinct idempotency key so the test measures exclusion between different requests rather than deduplication of one retry, and asserts exactly one admission plus a durable row count rather than merely the absence of an error. The zero-mutation clause is proven by counting rather than by asserting success, twice over: a `countingExecutor`/`countingBeginner` wrapping the real `dbport.Tx` (the pattern `internal/humanwork/workitem/decide_approval_test.go` established) requires every mutating statement a refused start issues to target `promotion_active_intent_guard` and nothing else, and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Security` additionally diffs row counts across `intent_instance`, `ledger_event`, `work_item` and the domain tables. The guard is proven to hold with the UI entirely out of the picture: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Security` calls `journeyEngine.Propose` directly with no HTTP, gRPC or page involved, and the PRIMARY calls `Admit` directly. Four pre-existing tests were updated rather than weakened, each of which had assumed two proposals for one worker's single effective date are both admitted -- the exact defect this todo closes. `TestTodo_PROMO_007_Integration`'s digest subtest now asserts the second request is refused with `journey.propose_promotion.active_conflict`, keeps its original content-digest claim by computing `app.PromotionProposeRequestDigest` on the refused request directly, and adds a row count proving no second intent was created; `TestTodo_PROMO_007_Mutation`, `TestTodo_WF_RUN_027_Bootstrap_Security` and `TestJourneyDecideRejectReachesTheRejectedTerminal` now use distinct, non-overlapping effective dates so their own zero-effect and terminal claims still exercise two genuinely admitted proposals. **Boundary, and it is a real one.** `promotionguard.Release` is implemented and unit-tested but is called from no production code, because no write-time hook fires when an intent reaches a terminal stage (`deriveJourneyStage` is read-time only, computed from workflow runtime nodes). A guard row is therefore created ACTIVE and never closed, so once a promotion is rejected or completed, re-proposing for that same worker and effective date is refused permanently; the workaround is a different effective date. This also disagrees with the UI, whose `activeConflict` signal still comes from the pre-existing `ListJourneys` non-terminal scan rather than the guard table, so after a journey goes terminal the UI offers Start while the server refuses it. RED frames the guard around a worker with a _nonterminal_ promotion, so blocking past terminal is outside the contract this todo was built for; escalated separately rather than left implied. Two registry rows were added during review that the lane could not write itself: `promotion_active_intent_guard`, and `ledger_payload_disposition`, which LEDGER-011 shipped without a `definitions/storage/storage-disposition.yaml` entry and which had left `TestTodo_DATA_001` red since that merge.

The concurrent double-approval is made impossible by the database rather than by a check that precedes the write. `Store.LockApprovalSiblings` issues `SELECT ... WHERE tenant_id AND proposal_ref AND kind='APPROVAL' ORDER BY work_item_id FOR UPDATE` inside the caller's own transaction; ordering by `work_item_id` means every caller acquires the same locks in the same order, so two racing completions cannot deadlock, and because both requirements on one proposal name the _same_ row set only one transaction can hold them. `approval.Complete` takes that lock before it reads any state and before the completing write, and holds it for the rest of the call, so the loser blocks until the winner commits and then observes the committed conflict and refuses with `ErrSeparationConflict`. `TestTodo_PROMOUX_003_Race` proves it with two real PostgreSQL connections and transactions released from a barrier, stable across five runs. RED's undifferentiated-owner clause is closed structurally rather than by convention: the new `approverclass` package derives provably distinct finance and manager principals from one base, and both `internal/platform/execution` and `internal/intent/app` route each requirement to its derived owner instead of the shared `principal:promotion-approver` the dev environment had been minting for both. Digest preservation under reassignment is proven by diff rather than by a non-empty check: the Integration test captures the full durable record, forces a real reassignment through the HRBP departure fallback, then requires `ProposalRef` equality plus field-by-field equality of tenant, item id, kind, work type, correlation, instance, node, requirement ref, policy route, visibility, org scope, deadline, created-at and subjects -- while asserting the owner actually moved, so the equality claim cannot pass vacuously. REFACTOR's clause that separation is evaluated by the approval owner rather than by whichever surface calls it is proven with the UI entirely absent: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_003_Security` drives a conflicted principal through `workitem.Store.DecideApproval` composed with the new `SeparationAuthority` driver -- no HTTP, no journey engine, no page -- and every PRIMARY and RACE subtest calls `approval.Complete` directly. `SeparationAuthority` fills the concrete `workitem.AuthorityRecheckPort` seam that EP-WORK-003 left unimplemented and whose absence was recorded as a boundary when that todo closed. Presentation consumes the disposition rather than recomputing it. `ApprovalDispositionProjectionFrom` is a pure field copy and `approvalDispositionCardProps` only localizes; no membership, authority or conflict logic exists in `productui`. The rendered card states the five facts GREEN names, and both the props and the rendered markup are asserted not to leak -- a candidate-set owner renders as a generic protected-group phrase with `candidates:` and `sha256:` required absent from the emitted HTML, and a conflicted viewer's refusal names no second principal. **Boundaries.** The disposition card was not observed on screen: the dev corpus holds no approval work items, so `/workspace/app/work` renders `0 items`, and the card is proven instead by asserting the real rendered HTML through `ui.RenderToString` on the same server-rendered path this page uses. The assigned-person label humanizes a raw principal reference because no directory lookup is reachable from `productui`; a real display name is a larger, separate feature. `SeparationAuthority` protects the domain capability rather than a live endpoint, because EP-WORK-003's transport still has no production completion wiring -- a pre-existing gap already escalated, neither created nor worsened here -- and `execute.Driver.CompleteApproval` inherits the guarantee but has no production caller. Separately, `TestTodo_DB_EDGE_003_IntegrationPromotionCompositionRetriesSerializableAndRechecksApproval` had a hardcoded 20s budget that turned machine load into a false failure; confirmed pre-existing by running it in a worktree of unmodified HEAD, where it failed identically at 22.9s and 32.4s, and raised to 120s with every assertion unchanged.

The server gate (`internal/transport/journey/diagnostics_access.go`) fails **closed**: a nil RoleAccess store, an empty permission table and an absent explicit grant all deny, deliberately unlike the pre-existing `requirePageAction`'s permissive rolling-upgrade default, because this authority never existed before and a permissive default would have silently granted it to everyone. The presence channel is closed by a server-derived `JourneyCard.DiagnosticsAuthorized` computed once via `cfg.CanPageAction("journey-diagnostics", "view")`, never from data presence; the detail page's `workflowSection`, `outcomeSection` and `evidenceSection`, which had rendered unconditionally whenever they held content, are gated the same way -- a defect the first evidence pass missed because it scanned only the list page. **Live matrix.** Signed in as the `admin` persona and again as a `promotion_operator`-only credential, `/workspace/app/journeys` renders 9 `Technical details` disclosures whose contents are redacted to `Worker ••••0020` and `Instance ••••9d08` with zero full UUIDs visible and two copy controls carrying the distinct accessible names `Copy Worker value` and `Copy Instance value`, the buttons writing the unredacted value through `navigator.clipboard.writeText`. Signed in as the `hiring-manager` persona (`hiring_manager`, `manager`, `intent_author`), the same page renders **0** disclosures, 0 UUIDs and 0 `eref:` occurrences in visible text, and every UUID remaining anywhere in the markup is a `href="#/journeys/<id>"` routing address -- a scan for a UUID outside an `href` attribute returned none. `/workspace/app/work` likewise fell from one raw UUID in visible text to zero for that persona. Because unauthorized viewers receive `detailsCount: 0` uniformly, there is no per-journey variation left to infer from. The `promotion_operator`-only run also answered the lane's one open question: `RoleAccess.Bootstrap`'s idempotent upsert does seed the new page id into an already-bootstrapped tenant on restart, so the grant is live without a manual migration. No pre-existing test file was edited. The clause that carries this todo is that an authority-filtered invalidation carries a sequence, and those two requirements interact as a disclosure bug rather than a cosmetic one: with a global sequence and a filter that merely drops undeliverable messages, a viewer who observes 1, 2, 4 has learned that event 3 exists and can count promotions they hold no authority over. The scheme chosen is gap-free renumbering per subscriber. `promotioninvalidation.NextSequence` allocates each committed transition a durable global position through `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE ... RETURNING`, evaluated inside each writer's own commit so concurrent writers cannot lose or duplicate one, but that value never reaches the wire -- it serves only as an item's revision for stale and reorder protection. `SubscriberSequencer.EmitForSubscriber` mints each subscriber its own counter and advances it by exactly one **only when a message is actually delivered**, so a transition authorising nothing for that subscriber never touches their counter and their visible sequence is contiguous by construction. The proof reproduces the leak before fixing it, which is what distinguishes it from a test that merely asserts the corrected behaviour: the PRIMARY's `subscriber_sequencer_closes_the_disclosure_gap_the_naive_scheme_leaks` subtest first runs the naive scheme and observes the delivered pair `[1, 3]` with a gap of 2, then runs the real one and requires `[1, 2]` with a delta of exactly 1. Region isolation is proven against real `tools/uxqual/invalidation.Client` instances rather than a stub: a Detail-region message for one worker fires exactly the matching client once and leaves a My-Work client and a different worker's Detail client at zero, so REFACTOR's prohibition on a full-shell reload is enforced rather than assumed. Last-updated is proven equal to the newest transition's own `OccurredAt` regardless of input order, with an empty set rendering an empty string rather than falling back to the current time. The no-duplicate-render clause is counted rather than inferred, because a double render converges to the same state and would pass any state assertion: the Recovery test counts `Refetch` invocations across a reconnect that redelivers an already-applied sequence before a genuinely new one, and requires exactly two. The Performance entry asserts delivered-message counts and bounded per-subscriber state rather than elapsed time, deliberately avoiding this machine's unreliable wall-clock behaviour. Zero values fail closed throughout: `RegionCursor{}` refuses any incoming value including 0, `Transition{}` and zero-revision or zero-timestamp variants fail `Validate()`, and the sequencer never advances on an undelivered message. **A defect I introduced was found by this lane and corrected here.** The `ledger_payload_disposition` row I added during PROMOUX-002 review declared `data_role: EVIDENCE` and `retention_class: EVIDENCE`, neither of which is a declared value -- `data_role` admits only LEDGER, PROJECTION, OUTBOX, REGISTRY, CONTROL and AGGREGATE, and `retention_class` only PERMANENT, OPERATIONAL and REBUILDABLE. It broke `TestTodo_STORE_001` and `TestTodo_STORE_001_Mutation` and had escaped notice because that gate lives in `internal/data/tenancy/storagedisposition`, a different package from the `TestTodo_DATA_001` check run at the time. Corrected to LEDGER and PERMANENT, matching `ledger_event` itself. **Boundaries.** The components are not wired into a live promotion page, the same boundary PROMOUX-003, 005, 006 and 007 recorded and which is escalated for all of them together; no production caller yet invokes `NextSequence` from a committed-transition write path, which lies outside this todo's Refs. DOM scroll and focus preservation on reconnect is asserted structurally -- region containers are independently addressable -- because it cannot be proven in a non-browser Go test, and the Recovery test says so in its own comment.

- [ ] `PROMOUX-013` **[PHASE_3][SOL_HIGH] Add governed edit, supersede, withdraw and cancel paths.**
  - **Audit (2026-09-24):** Reopened: declared Mutation and Recovery matrix tests are absent, and no completed evidence proves the full served lifecycle contract. Keep open until the missing named proofs and literal GREEN are satisfied.
  - **Depends:** `INTENT-005`, `WF-RUN-015`, `WEB-122`, `WEB-132`.
  - **INTENT CONTEXT:** `ROLE=GOVERNANCE; SETS=BI.PEOPLE,BI.REWARDS; INTENTS=PromoteWorker; DIRECT=none; WHY=let authorized actors correct or stop a promotion without mutating immutable proposal history`.
  - **TEST:** `TestTodo_PROMOUX_013`.
  - **TEST MATRIX:** `PRIMARY=TestTodo_PROMOUX_013`; `INTEGRATION=TestTodo_PROMOUX_013_Integration`; `BROWSER=TestTodo_PROMOUX_013_Browser`; `SECURITY=TestTodo_PROMOUX_013_Security`; `RECOVERY=TestTodo_PROMOUX_013_Recovery`; `MUTATION=TestTodo_PROMOUX_013_Mutation`.
  - **RED:** a proposer cannot correct an unstarted proposal, withdraw before approval, or request cancellation during an eligible wait; or an edit silently changes an approved revision.
  - **GREEN:** authorized edits create a new proposal revision and invalidate material approvals; withdrawal and cancellation use typed interventions with reasons, consequence preview and retained evidence; unavailable stages explain why; races with approval, timer and terminal commit resolve to one deterministic outcome with no partial domain write.

Three RPCs were added to `JourneyService` -- `EditProposal`, `PreviewJourneyIntervention` (read-only) and `RequestJourneyIntervention` -- each carrying the file's own `Effect class:` disposition comment verified through a descriptor-based totality test, plus a shared `hcmnext.common.v1.InterventionOutcome` enum (`APPLIED|PENDING_SAFE_POINT|DENIED|TOO_LATE|REPAIR_REQUIRED`) and `Journey.governance_version`, the intent's own optimistic-concurrency version, which nothing on this wire exposed before. `buf generate` is byte-identical across two runs and touches only the three expected files, independently reproduced at review time by regenerating and comparing digests. The wire change was necessary because `DecideJourneyRequest` carried only `{intent_id, approve bool, reason}` -- an approve/reject binary with no room for withdraw, cancel, supersede or edit. **The implementation reused the existing domain capability rather than reimplementing it, and discovering that `SupersedeIntent` could not be reused at all was the key finding.** `promote_worker` is P1A/`simulateOnlyChangeTransitions`, whose `SUPERSEDED` edges exist only from `SIMULATED`, `SUBMITTED` or `APPROVED`; a journey's stored intent never durably leaves `DRAFT`, and the kernel's own lifecycle profile has no `DRAFT` to `SUPERSEDED` edge, so `SupersedeIntent` is structurally unusable here. `EditProposal` therefore composes `CancelIntent` -- legal from `DRAFT` and already safe-point-aware for a mid-flight `EXECUTING` journey -- followed by an ordinary `Propose` once the cancellation disposition is genuinely `CANCELLED`, which makes GREEN's requirement that edits create a new proposal revision and invalidate material approvals literally true: the original carries the approval, the original is what is durably cancelled, and the successor inherits nothing. **Three real defects were found by running the code rather than reasoning about it, each observed failing before the fix and passing after.** `lifecycle_endpoints.go`'s `SupersedeIntent` minted and durably appended the successor intent before validating and applying the original's own transition, so a refused or raced supersede left an orphaned successor behind -- a genuine partial write, now reordered so the original's compare-and-swap lands first. `journey_decide.go`'s `Decide` and `Execute` checked no terminal `RequestState`, so a journey cancelled mid-flight could still be decided or executed; both now carry a terminal-state guard. And `internal/data/promotionguard.Release` was dead code by its own doc comment, so a cancelled-then-reproposed journey for the same worker and effective date would have refused itself as a duplicate; it is now called on a successful `CANCELLED` disposition. `TestTodo_PROMOUX_013_Race` drives 8 concurrent goroutines -- 4 `EditProposal`, 4 `RequestJourneyIntervention(WITHDRAW)` -- through the production connection pool against one real proposed journey, all presenting the same expected version, and asserts durable state rather than return codes: exactly one successor intent exists if an edit won and zero if a withdraw won, which is what would have caught the orphaned-successor defect directly. The UI is wired end to end rather than left as an unreachable capability: `reviewSurface` needed no changes because PROMOUX-010's prop contract was deliberately built to accommodate Withdraw and Cancel, so this was plumbing through `journeyclient`, and Withdraw, Cancel and Edit render at every stage -- disabled with a named reason when unavailable rather than omitted, since an omitted action is indistinguishable from one that does not exist. `interventionNotice` reports the typed outcome truthfully instead of always claiming cancellation. The disclosure rule is proven by value in the I18N test, which asserts the disabled-reason text is byte-identical across two journeys sharing a terminal stage but differing in worker name and correlation id -- the same pattern PROMOUX-001 and PROMOUX-004 established. **A client-side mirror of the server's stage-availability rule was accepted but required a test, and the lane was sent back for it.** `journeyclient.InterventionAvailability` mirrors `internal/intent/app`'s unexported `interventionUnavailableAtStage` so availability cannot go stale between watch pushes; it is a presentation hint rather than an authorization decision, since the server refuses on submit regardless, but an untested mirror drifts silently and the failure mode is a user confidently told an action is unavailable when it is not. `TestTodo_PROMOUX_013_ClientServerAvailabilityAgreement` now runs both implementations across the full cross product of 15 stages by 2 kinds, reading the stage and kind lists from the generated enums' own `_name` maps rather than a hardcoded list so a newly added stage fails the test instead of being silently skipped, with a hard failure if either map is empty or names a kind the test does not cover; all 30 pairs agree on both availability and reason reference. Mutation-verified by dropping `stageBlocked` from the client's unstarted check, which failed exactly two pairs by name -- `WITHDRAW at BLOCKED` and `CANCEL at BLOCKED` -- while the other 28 kept passing. The three UI tests were each mutation-verified too: dropping `DisabledReason` failed the BROWSER naming `disabled action "withdraw" has no reason paragraph`; renaming the reason field's label and dropping `Required` failed the ACCESSIBILITY naming `no visible label "Reason" found`; and forcing the static description in place of the server preview failed the I18N naming that the server-worded consequence summary did not survive rendering byte-for-byte. **Boundaries, recorded rather than glossed.** The I18N test proves the plumbing survives translated and bidi content but does not prove localized delivery, because `tools/uxqual/render/journey` has no locale catalog and emits no `dir="rtl"` anywhere -- every string including PROMOUX-010's is fixed English Go source, and building that catalog is a separate and much larger effort. Consequence previews refresh on detail load and after an intervention rather than on every watch tick, so the server's worded consequence sentence has a bounded staleness window; availability and reason text never go stale, being computed from the always-fresh stage. Edit's job-code and base-pay fields pre-fill from display strings rather than parsed values, which is cosmetic because the reviewer retypes them. `EP-WF-002` was deliberately not implemented, but `InterventionOutcome` and `workspace.JourneyInterventionOutcome` are placed in shared locations specifically so its Pause, Resume, Cancel and RetryNode work can adopt the same five-value vocabulary rather than inventing a second one. **One infrastructure landmine was found and independently reproduced:** `buf.gen.yaml` declares `clean: true` over the whole `gen/go` tree, which also holds `gen/go/hcmnext/model/model_generated.go`, a non-buf output from `tools/gen/modelgen`, so every `buf generate` silently deletes it -- verified at review time by running `buf generate` and watching the file disappear, then restoring it byte-identical with `go run ./tools/gen/modelgen/cmd/modelgen`. That is the true cause of a phantom missing-`gen/go/hcmnext/model` build failure another lane hit earlier the same day, which was initially misattributed to a concurrency race. It needs a permanent fix -- a combined regeneration script or a separate output root -- and is filed separately rather than patched here.

  - **Depends:** `WEB-023`, `WEB-037`, `WEB-047`, `UXAUDIT-008`.
  - **INTENT CONTEXT:** `ROLE=EXPOSURE; SETS=BI.EXPERIENCE; DIRECT=none; WHY=preserve navigation, context and focus while large server-backed regions scroll`.

  - **RED:** navigation scrolls with page content, page and table compete for the same gesture, horizontal overflow is hidden, sticky headers detach from columns, popovers create accidental body scroll, or a styled scrollbar intrudes into content.
  - **GREEN:** the shell, navigation, page, table, drawer and overlay declare noncompeting scroll ownership; sticky headers and action bars remain within their container; focus is never hidden; keyboard, wheel, touch and RTL horizontal scrolling work; scrollbar size, contrast, gutter and edge placement use theme tokens and meet target requirements.

  - **Refs:** [frontend plan](specs/production-frontend-and-page-composition.md), `tools/uxqual/render/journey`, `tools/uxqual/productclient`.
  - **Evidence (2026-09-13):** `TestTodo_UIPOLISH_004` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_UIPOLISH_004_Browser`, `TestTodo_UIPOLISH_004_Accessibility`, `TestTodo_UIPOLISH_004_Performance` and `TestTodo_UIPOLISH_004_Regression` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`todo_uipolish_004_test.go`); no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/humanwork/productui/` PASS at 93.4%; `go build ./...` clean on windows/arm64 and cross-checked clean under `GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64`, `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build ./tools/uxqual/cmd/journeywasm/` clean, `go vet` and gofmt clean on every touched file; branch main. **RED reproduced live before the change** at 1440x900 on `/workspace/app/people`: three scroll regions were configured ad hoc and disagreed with each other. `.main-scroll` computed `scrollbar-width: auto` with `scrollbar-color: auto` -- a 15px native bar -- against `.primary-nav` and `.data-table-scroll` both using `thin` plus a themed token, and it carried no `role`, no `tabindex` and no accessible name at all while scrolling 466px, so a keyboard user could not reach it. `.action-launcher-dialog` was a fourth untokenized region. **Verified live after the change**, rebuilding the wasm bundle then the server binary in that order: all five regions now render through one `ScrollRegion` component and agree -- `.main-scroll` at `thin` with a themed `scrollbar-color`, `tabindex="0"` and an accessible name resolved through `aria-labelledby` to the page heading; `.primary-nav` (`Main`), `.sidebar` (`Workspace navigation`) and `.data-table-scroll` (`Authorized people`) all `thin`, tokenized and focusable; `.action-launcher-dialog` tokenized and named `Go to`, deliberately not focusable itself because focus belongs on its input under the standard ARIA dialog pattern. **UXAUDIT-008's matched pair survived the consolidation**, which was the main regression risk: `.data-table-scroll` still computes `max-height: 738px` together with `overflow-y: auto` in the same context, its `th` still `sticky`, 20 rows rendered -- the pairing whose split clipped 16 workers unreachably earlier the same day, and the rule-level invariant test still guards it. Three RED clauses did not reproduce and were deliberately left alone rather than rebuilt: scroll chaining is already prevented because all regions compute `overscroll-behavior: contain`; `html` and `body` both compute `overflow: hidden`, so popovers cannot create accidental body scroll; and sticky headers do not detach, proven in UXAUDIT-008 by 0px column drift across all six columns scrolled fully right and 200px down. `.main-scroll` keeps `overflow-x: hidden` as a deliberate decision -- every region beneath it that can need horizontal scroll owns its own, and a regression test pins `.data-table-scroll` keeping horizontal overflow so wide content cannot be stranded by the shell's hidden axis. All five tests were mutation-verified against a real break and observed failing before restore: removing `scrollbar-width` from the new `.main-scroll` rule failed the PRIMARY naming the missing token; setting `Focusable: false` on `.main-scroll` failed the BROWSER with `page region ... is not keyboard-focusable`; removing the `Aria` map from `.sidebar` failed the ACCESSIBILITY with `element has no accessible name`; rendering a duplicate region with the same id failed the PERFORMANCE with `id="data-table-scroll" occurrences = 2, want exactly 1`; and reintroducing UXAUDIT-008's exact broken pairing failed the REGRESSION with the same message its own historical comment records. **Boundaries, named rather than glossed.** A shared `scroll-region` marker class was deliberately not added to the DOM -- a first attempt broke roughly eight pre-existing tests that assert exact `class=` values -- so the five regions are reached through one comma-joined selector list built from an exported `ScrollRegionSelectors` list instead, keeping the single source of truth in Go without changing rendered markup. Scroll-edge shadows are scoped only to `.data-table-scroll`, which is already `position: relative`; adding `position: relative` blind to the other four risked changing the containing block for an unaudited absolutely-positioned descendant. The shell itself owns no `ScrollRegion` because its contract is to declare no scroll of its own and defer to the five, which an existing test already pins. `scroll_restoration_wasm_test.go` compiles under `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm` but this repository's CI never executes wasm tests, so only its compilation is proven. Two golden shell digests were re-pinned for the new `tabindex`/`id` attributes after diffing the rendered markup and confirming only the intended attributes changed.

The History filter stack no longer inherits desktop 150px/280px flex-basis as mobile control height: its single-column grid restores compact 44px selects, checked manually at 390px in RTL Arabic with populated records. The table/form/object, density-preference and full viewport/accessibility/performance matrix remain open.

## 73. Workflow engine plan-vs-implementation gaps (2026-09-14)

A read-only review of [the workflow runtime spec](specs/workflow-runtime.md) against the served implementation found the kernel libraries largely built but a narrow, partly stubbed production path. These todos cover gaps no existing todo tracks; ticked todos the code did not satisfy were reopened in place with a dated note. A checkbox requires the named tests and proof on the composed serve path, not a library-only harness.

The propose path selects the OPEN target position deterministically and submits it as the picker-issued `position.RevisionRef` PROMOUX-004 re-derives existence, compatibility and vacancy from (`internal/intent/app/promotion_target_position.go`), carries the approved annualized base pay as a planned write in simcomp's own field path and pins the unchanged manager as an identical current/proposed assertion pair rather than a write (`proposal_commit_material.go`), and holds the raise against the unit's pool as a DB-010 `budget_reservation` recorded no later than the revision's `ProducedAt` (`internal/data/promotionbudget`), released by every terminal fact and by a governed cancellation. Each approval records its GOVERN-002 decision durably (migration 00309 `promotion_approval_governance`, append-only, tenant RLS: the composed `decision.Inputs`, the decision and its digest, the seven GOVERN-003 facts as the durable stores reported them, and the plan digest the decision authorized), built by the same construction `Revalidate` uses so an unchanged world reproduces the digest exactly. The core's earlier commit is never touched or rolled back, and a failed downstream leg no longer either aborts the advance (leaving a RUNNING instance with nothing to run and the committed outcome masked behind an error) or refuses `NO_FAILURE_ROUTE`. `TestTodo_WF_RUN_037`, `_Property`, `_Fault` and `_Conformance` pass with the workflow, execute, runtime, platform/execution, promotionexec, simulate and conformance suites on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3). The promotion plan's digest changes with the added roles, so the pinned plan digest moves with this change.
